Its inputs include four 8-bit data sources, a 2-bit address-select, write and output enables, and a clock; the 10-bit data bus is bidirectional. Address logic selects among the immediate value, stack pointer, decremented stack pointer, or register-file value. When write enable is high, the selected address is loaded from the data bus; when output enable is high, the memory asynchronously drives the bus, otherwise it is high-impedance.

This module reads MPU6050 sensor data over I2C and indicates axis/sign results on LEDs. Its ports are MCLK and RESET inputs, open-drain I2C SDA/SCL, and LEDX/LEDY/LEDZ/LEDSIGN outputs. Internally, a counter derives a periodic TIC strobe, while an I2C master and MPU6050 controller manage bus transfers to device address 0x68. When LOAD and TIC coincide, 8-bit data at addresses 0, 2, and 4 are latched into XREG/YREG/ZREG. A COMPARE block uses these registers to drive the LED outputs.

This module is a combinational 8-bit incrementer. It takes an 8-bit input `count` and produces an 8-bit output `nextCount`. The output equals the input plus one, with overflow wrapping modulo 256. Since it is purely combinational, there is no clock or reset.

This module is a dual-clock, 8-bit register whose value is controlled by two independent rising-edge clock domains. Its inputs are clk1 and clk2; its only output is out1, an 8-bit wire. Internally, one 8-bit register is updated to 1 on each clk1 rising edge and to 3 on each clk2 rising edge, while out1 continuously mirrors that register. There is no reset, and because both clocked blocks write the same register, coincident edges cause a race and the design is generally not synthesizable.

This module implements a positive-edge-triggered D flip-flop with an asynchronous active-high reset. Its inputs are a data input, a clock, and a reset; its output is the registered value. When reset is asserted, the output is cleared to zero immediately, regardless of the clock. Otherwise, on each rising clock edge, the output captures and stores the current data input. Reset therefore has priority over normal data loading.
Response:
module dff(
input wire d,
input wire clk,
input wire reset,
output reg q
);
  always @(posedge clk, posedge reset) begin
    if((reset == 1'b1)) begin
      q <= 1'b0;
    end else begin
      q <= d;
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module is a clock source multiplexer that routes either a bypass clock or a PLL-derived clock (1x, 2x, or 4x) to clkout. It has a 2-bit clksel input, a testen input, and clock inputs clkin, clk1x, clk2x, clk4x; clkout is the single output. Internally, test mode is enabled only when testen and the scantest parameter are both asserted. A bypass select is generated for clksel=00 or test mode, and mutually exclusive select signals choose clk1x, clk2x, or clk4x otherwise. Three cascaded clkmux blocks implement the final selection.

This module is a 3-bit equality comparator. It has one output, eq, and two 3-bit inputs, in0 and in1. Internally, it checks whether the two inputs differ, producing a low result when they are unequal and a high result when they match. That comparison result drives the eq output. The module contains no sequential state or clocking.

This module is a synchronous rising-edge detector that produces a one-clock-cycle pulse on VYSTUP whenever input VSTUP transitions from low to high. Its ports are CLK (clock input), VSTUP (signal input), and VYSTUP (registered pulse output). Internally, a flip-flop stores the previous VSTUP value; an XOR gate flags any change, and an AND gate with VSTUP isolates only low-to-high transitions. A second flip-flop registers that pulse, aligning VYSTUP to the clock edge.

Top-level brute-force MD5 password cracker. It takes clk, active-low rstn, a data-receive strobe, and a 128-bit target hash, and outputs a found flag plus the recovered 48-bit password. A controller sequences a string generator, pre-processor, MD5 core, and comparator: candidate strings are padded, hashed, and compared against the target. When equal, the controller asserts o_pw_found and drives the matching password on o_passwd.
Response:
module brutus_top(
input wire clk,
input wire rstn,
input wire i_fsl_data_recv,
input wire [127:0] i_fsl_hash,
output wire o_pw_found,
output wire [47:0] o_passwd
);
parameter [31:0] M=1;
wire [2:0] s_len_sg_pp;  // length sg->pp
wire [7:0] s_len_pp_md5;  // length pp->md5
wire [47:0] s_string_sg_pp;
wire [31:0] s_string1_pp_md5;
wire [31:0] s_string2_pp_md5;
wire [31:0] h0; wire [31:0] h1; wire [31:0] h2; wire [31:0] h3;  // hashes from md5 to comparator
wire comp_ctrl_eq; wire sg_ctrl_done; wire md5_ctrl_done;
wire [47:0] sg_ctrl_string;
wire [127:0] ctrl_comp_hash;
wire ctrl_sg_comp_start;  // start signal to sg and comp
wire ctrl_md5_start;  // start signal to MD5 cores
wire ctrl_sg_halt;  // halt signal to sg
wire [M - 1:0] ctrl_demux_sel; wire [M - 1:0] ctrl_mux_sel;  // mux/demux selectors
  controller #(
      .N(M))
  controller_inst(
      .clk(clk),
    .rstn(rstn),
    .i_fsl_data_recv(i_fsl_data_recv),
    .i_fsl_hash(i_fsl_hash),
    .i_comp_eq(comp_ctrl_eq),
    .i_sg_done(sg_ctrl_done),
    .i_sg_string(sg_ctrl_string),
    .i_md5_done(md5_ctrl_done),
    .o_passwd_hash(ctrl_comp_hash),
    .o_pw_found(o_pw_found),
    .o_passwd(o_passwd),
    .o_start_sg_comp(ctrl_sg_comp_start),
    .o_start_md5(ctrl_md5_start),
    .o_halt_sg(ctrl_sg_halt),
    .o_demux_sel(/* open */),
    .o_mux_sel(/* open */));
  comp comp_inst(
      .clk(clk),
    .rstn(rstn),
    .i_cmp_hash(i_fsl_hash),
    .i_hash_0(h0),
    .i_hash_1(h1),
    .i_hash_2(h2),
    .i_hash_3(h3),
    .i_start(ctrl_sg_comp_start),
    .o_equal(comp_ctrl_eq));
  assign sg_ctrl_string = s_string_sg_pp;
  // string goes both to pp and controller
  string_generator sg_inst(
      .clk(clk),
    .rstn(rstn),
    .i_start(ctrl_sg_comp_start),
    .i_halt(ctrl_sg_halt),
    .o_done(sg_ctrl_done),
    .o_length(s_len_sg_pp),
    .o_string(s_string_sg_pp));
  pre_process pp_inst(
      .i_data(s_string_sg_pp),
    .i_length(s_len_sg_pp),
    .o_data_0(s_string1_pp_md5),
    .o_data_1(s_string2_pp_md5),
    .o_length(s_len_pp_md5));
  MD5 MD5_inst(
      .clk(clk),
    .rstn(rstn),
    .i_start(ctrl_md5_start),
    .i_data_0(s_string1_pp_md5),
    .i_data_1(s_string2_pp_md5),
    .i_length(s_len_pp_md5),
    .o_done(md5_ctrl_done),
    .o_hash_0(h0),
    //o_hash(31 downto 0),
    .o_hash_1(h1),
    //o_hash(63 downto 32),
    .o_hash_2(h2),
    //o_hash(95 downto 64),
    .o_hash_3(h3));
endmodule

Instruction: This module implements a serial-controlled logic-analyzer top level. Its ports include reset, crystal and external clocks, a 32-bit probe input, UART receive/transmit, two switches, and an 8-bit LED output. A clock manager derives the system clock, while an EIA-232 block handles serial commands and data transfer. The core samples the probe input on the external clock and accesses a block-RAM buffer using read/write signals; LEDs mirror status signals.

This module implements a single-bit combinational buffer. It has one input, `i_foo`, and one output, `o_foo`. Internally, the input is routed through an intermediate wire and combined with a constant zero using XOR, so the output simply follows the input. There is no clocked or sequential behavior.

SimpleUnitReanamedPort0 is a purely combinational module that acts as a direct connection between its input and output. It has one single-bit input, `a_in_hdl`, and one single-bit output, `b`. Internally, the output is continuously assigned the input value, so `b` follows `a_in_hdl` exactly. It performs no computation, inversion, storage, clocking, or reset behavior.

This module is an 8-bit equality comparator. It takes two 8-bit inputs, A and B, and produces a single-bit output EQ. EQ is high when A and B are identical, and low when they differ. The logic is purely combinational, with no clock or stored state, so EQ follows input changes immediately.

The module is a switch-controlled logic demonstrator: four submodules compute candidate 4-bit results from the lower switches, and a 4-to-1 multiplexer selects one based on SW[9:8]. Inputs are the 10-bit slide-switch bus SW; outputs are the 7-segment display HEX0 and the 10-bit LED register LEDR. Internally, C1–C3 each combine SW[3:0] and SW[7:4], while C4 uses only SW[3:0], yielding F1–F4. The selected nibble F is decoded to HEX0, and LEDR shows F in its low four bits with the upper six bits cleared.

This module is a 41-bit subtractor and signed comparator. It takes two 41-bit operands, in_a and in_b, plus a sign control input, and produces a 41-bit difference along with ge (greater-or-equal) and le (less-or-equal) flags. Internally it zero-extends both operands and performs a 43-bit subtraction, taking the middle bits as the result. Comparison outputs are derived from the operands’ sign bits, the subtraction carry, and the sign input.

This module acts as an 8-bit pass-through, directly connecting its input to its output. It has an 8-bit output `o1` and an 8-bit input `i1`, but the input is declared with opposite index ordering. Internally, a continuous assignment copies the input bit pattern to the output without inversion or modification. The differing index ranges do not alter the transferred value. No other logic is present.

The module is intended as a constant ROM that outputs successive 8-bit slices of a parameter on each clock. It has a clock input and an 8-bit registered output. Inside, an index counter increments each cycle until it reaches 12, then resets to 0, cycling through thirteen values. The output is a part-select of the parameter C_IEND, using the current index to choose the 8-bit slice. However, C_IEND is declared as only one bit wide, so the part-select is out of range and the design would not behave as intended without widening that parameter.

A 16×16-bit radix-4 Booth multiplier that produces a truncated 16-bit product slice. It takes 16-bit inputs a and b, and drives the 16-bit output o from bits 29:14 of the full 32-bit internal product. Internally, a is zero-extended and split into eight overlapping 3-bit Booth-encoded groups. Each group feeds a Booth partial-product generator using b. The eight sign-extended partial products are then combined by a reduction block to form the internal product.

This module is a combinational hexadecimal-to-seven-segment decoder. It takes a 4-bit input `sw` and produces a 7-bit output `sevenseg`. An always block uses a case statement to map each hex digit 0 through E to a fixed segment pattern, with the default case covering F. The output changes whenever the input changes.

This module is a combinational Hamming encode/decode wrapper: it encodes a 32-bit input and immediately decodes it back to 32 bits. Its ports are a 32-bit data input, a 32-bit decoded data output, and three status outputs: single-error (se), double-error (de), and no-error (ne). Internally, an encoder produces a 39-bit Hamming codeword that feeds a decoder. The decoder regenerates the 32-bit output and drives the three error-status flags from its internal error signals.

Sample packer converting a stream of 64-bit words (four 12-bit samples each) into 192-bit groups re-packed as three 64-bit outputs per four inputs. Inputs: clk, rst, enable, data_in_dval, 64-bit data_in, data_out_stop; outputs: data_in_stop, data_out_dval, 64-bit data_out. A 2-bit cycle counter tracks position, a history register holds the prior word, and a case statement concatenates current and stored 12-bit fields into each output word, with valid asserted on cycles 2–4. data_in_stop mirrors data_out_stop; when enable is low, packing is bypassed.

ALU_ram is a control wrapper connecting an ALU result, a register file, and a RAM, selected by a 2-bit operand code. Inputs are clk, rst, a 4-bit register address, an 8-bit memory address, an 8-bit ALU result, and the 2-bit operand. Outputs drive register write data/address/enable, memory read/write enables, and memory read data. Internally it instantiates a RAM and uses combinational logic to perform no-op, register write of the ALU result, register load from memory, or memory store of the result. Reset and debug signals feed the RAM and expose memory control.

This top-level keyboard controller interfaces a PS/2 keyboard to an ASCII output. Its inputs are CLK and RST, while PS2_CLK and PS2_DATA are bidirectional PS/2 lines. It outputs an 8-bit ASCII_OUT, plus ASCII_RD (data ready) and ASCII_WE (write enable). Internally, a PS/2 driver handles the serial protocol and produces received data; a keycode-to-ASCII converter translates that data and asserts ASCII_RD; a final block generates ASCII_WE. The converted ASCII value drives ASCII_OUT, and unused transmit/error signals are tied low.

This module is an intended clock divider that generates a 2 Hz square wave from a 50 MHz input clock using a 24-bit prescaler. Its inputs are `clk_50Mhz` and an active-high asynchronous reset `rst`; its output is `clk_2Hz`. On reset, the prescaler and output register clear; otherwise the prescaler increments on each rising edge, and when it reaches `8'h10` it resets and toggles the output register, which drives `clk_2Hz`. Note the compare value 16 yields roughly 1.47 MHz, not 2 Hz.

Implements a 4-bit binary adder/subtractor selected by control input fnc. Inputs are 4-bit operands a and b plus fnc; output s_or_d is the 4-bit result. Internally, each b bit is XORed with fnc to optionally invert b, and four full adders form a ripple-carry chain whose initial carry-in is fnc. When fnc is 0, it computes a+b; when fnc is 1, it computes a-b via two's complement. The final carry out is discarded.

This module is a pipeline register that captures and delays a bundle of control and datapath signals. It takes Clk, Reset, and parallel inputs such as ncwp, call, if, rfsource, wrenmen, pcsource, aluop, a18, crs1out, op2out, PCC, RD, and Cuentrada, producing registered outputs of the same names with out suffixes. On each rising edge, Reset forces all outputs to zero; otherwise the inputs are copied to the outputs. The always block's sensitivity list includes every input signal, making it behave as a broad edge-triggered register.

This module is a 16-bit combinational logical unit that performs bitwise operations on two operands selected by a 3-bit opcode. Its inputs are 16-bit RA and RB and a 3-bit OP; its outputs are the 16-bit result LOG_OUT and a 4-bit status word SREG_OUT. Internal case logic selects OR, AND (also used for ANDI), or pass-through of RB for MOV, defaulting to OR. The status output places a zero flag in bit 2, set when the result is zero, with the remaining bits cleared.

This module is a combinational instruction decoder that translates an 8-bit instruction into one-hot execution control signals. Its input is `instruction_in`, with the upper four bits used as the opcode, and its outputs are fourteen individual flags such as NOP, STA, LDA, arithmetic/logic operations, jumps, and HLT.

Internally, all outputs are first cleared and then a priority `if-else` chain asserts exactly one output based on the opcode value, covering opcodes for NOP, STA, LDA, ADD, OR, AND, NOT, JMP, JN, JZ, HLT, SHR, SHL, and MUL. Any opcode not explicitly handled leaves all execution flags deasserted. The module is purely combinational, with no clock or reset.

This module implements a simple 32-bit program counter interface that currently acts as a pass-through. It has a 32-bit input, `programCounterIn`, and a 32-bit output, `programCounterOut`. Internally, the output is continuously assigned directly from the input, making the logic purely combinational with no clock or stored state. A comment suggests possible reset or scaling behavior, but that behavior is not implemented.

This module is a top-level controller that coordinates global run logic, a conveyor, and a box dropper. Its inputs include clock, reset, enable, sync, conveyor moving/jammed status, and global run/infinite-run/fault signals; its outputs are the conveyor run command, box dropper run command, and an overall done flag. Internally it instantiates three submodules: Globals_SIFB manages global run state and emits a run-changed event plus run and infinite-run data, while Conveyor_SIFB and BoxDropper_SIFB consume those signals to control their outputs. The done output is asserted only when all three submodules report completion.

This module has no meaningful function; it simply exposes an undriven output with no logic to determine its value. Its only port is a single output signal, with no inputs, clocks, or resets. Internally, a local wire is declared but never assigned, and that undriven wire is connected directly to the output. As a result, the output remains high-impedance rather than carrying a defined logic level.

This module is a clock divider that generates a periodic one-clock-wide time-base pulse from a faster input clock. Its ports are a clock input (in_clk), an asynchronous active-high reset (in_rst), and a registered output (out_time_base). Parameters FOSC and FDIV define the division ratio, with the terminal count CTAMAX equal to FOSC/FDIV. Internally, a 32-bit counter increments on each clock edge and is cleared asynchronously on reset; when the count reaches CTAMAX it wraps to zero and drives the output high for a single cycle, otherwise holding the output low.

This module conditionally routes input values to three outputs using combinational sensitivity to a, b, and c. It has three 1-bit inputs (a, b, c) and three 1-bit reg outputs (d, e, f). When a is high, d is assigned b; otherwise d is forced low. When both a and b are high, e receives c and f is cleared to zero. If that nested condition is false, e and f are not assigned, so they retain their previous values.
Response:
module SimpleIfStatementMergable2(
input wire a,
input wire b,
input wire c,
output reg d,
output reg e,
output reg f
);
  always @(a, b, c) begin
    if(a == 1'b1) begin
      d <= b;
      if(b == 1'b1) begin
        e <= c;
        f <= 1'b0;
      end
    end
    else begin
      d <= 1'b0;
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module implements a 4-to-1 multiplexer that routes one bit from a 4-bit input to a single output based on a 2-bit select. Its ports are a 2-bit select input, a 4-bit data input, and a single-bit registered output. The always block is level-sensitive to both select and data, making the design combinational. It compares the select value and assigns output bits 0 through 3 for select values 00, 01, 10, and 11 respectively. An internally declared wire is unused and does not affect behavior.

This module implements a simple 8-bit synchronous register. Its ports are a clock, a reset input, an 8-bit data input, and an 8-bit registered output. On each rising clock edge, the internal register loads the input value unless reset is asserted, which clears it to zero. The output continuously reflects the stored register value.

This module implements a 32-bit-wide 2-to-1 multiplexer. It has two 32-bit data inputs, x and y, a 1-bit select input, sel, and a 32-bit output, z. When sel is high, the output equals y; otherwise, it equals x. The design is purely combinational.

This module implements a purely combinational 32-bit adder. It takes two 32-bit inputs, INPUT_1 and INPUT_2, and produces one 32-bit output, OUTPUT_1. The output is continuously driven by the sum of the two inputs. There is no clock, reset, or stored state.

This module implements a 16×16 signed multiplier using radix-4 Booth encoding. It takes two 16-bit inputs, a and b, and produces a 16-bit output, o, which is the middle slice (bits 23:8) of the full 32-bit product. Internally, a is extended with a trailing zero to form a 17-bit value, then split into eight overlapping 3-bit groups that drive eight Booth partial-product generators. Each partial product is sign-extended and fed to a reduction block that sums them into the full product.

This module synchronizes and debounces a single-bit input. Inputs are rst, clk, en, and din; outputs are dout plus registered redge and fedge flags. Internally, din passes through two enabled flip-flops, and a counter runs while the synchronized value differs from the held output. When the counter reaches CNTFULL, dout updates and redge/fedge indicate the new level. Reset clears the counter, output, and flags.

This module implements a 16-bit-wide 4-to-1 multiplexer. It has a 2-bit select input SEL, four 16-bit data inputs DATA_0 through DATA_3, and a 16-bit output OUTPUT. Combinational logic evaluates SEL and forwards the selected data input to OUTPUT. For SEL values 00, 01, 10, and 11, it selects DATA_0, DATA_1, DATA_2, or DATA_3 respectively; the default case drives OUTPUT to zero.

This module is a top-level 1-to-N DDR single-ended receiver that deserializes eight input lanes into a 64-bit word. It has an active-high reset, 8-bit datain, two single-ended clocks clkin1/clkin2, and a 64-bit dummy_out. Internally, a clock block generates I/O clocks and a serdes strobe, while a data block deserializes the lanes with phase detection. A small bitslip state machine looks for a 4-bit pattern in the upper nibble and pulses bitslip for alignment, then the received word is registered to the output.

Wraps a GTX transceiver, converting between 16-bit parallel data and serial differential lines. Inputs: clk_i reference clock, rst_i reset, rxp_i/rxn_i serial receive pair, loopback_i, and 16-bit tx_data_i with tx_isk_i. Outputs: txp_o/txn_o serial transmit pair, 16-bit rx_data_o with rx_isk_o, clk_o user clock, and ready_o. A BUFG buffers the transceiver TX output clock into the shared RX/TX user clock; reference clock and loopback are zero-extended into the core. ready_o combines RX PLL lock and RX/TX reset-done.

This module implements a 4-bit modulo-16 up counter. It has a clock input CLK, an active-high synchronous reset input, and a 4-bit output Q_UP. On each rising clock edge, the internal register loads 4'b1111 when reset is high; otherwise it increments by one, wrapping from 15 to 0. The register value is continuously driven onto Q_UP.

This module computes the 32-bit difference of two 32-bit inputs, effectively `in_a - in_b` modulo 2^32. It has one 32-bit output `result` and two 32-bit inputs `in_a` and `in_b`. Internally, both inputs are zero-extended and shifted left by one bit before subtraction, and the middle 32 bits of the 34-bit difference are selected as the output. The extra low bit is discarded, while the extra high bit provides borrow/sign handling.

This module is a combinational 4-bit to 7-segment display decoder. Its input is a 4-bit value `e`, and its output is a 7-bit segment pattern `s`. The internal logic is a single continuous assignment using nested conditional operators to map input values 0 through 8 to their corresponding display patterns. Inputs above 8 are not handled, as the final conditional branch is incomplete, leaving those outputs unassigned.

This module implements a single-bit D flip-flop. Its ports are a clock input, an active-low asynchronous reset input, a data input, and a registered output. Internally, one register stores the value and continuously drives the output. When reset is asserted it should asynchronously clear the register to zero, otherwise it loads the data input. However, the sensitivity list triggers on the rising edge of reset rather than the falling edge, so the intended asynchronous reset behavior is not correctly implemented.

This module is the receive data path for a serial receiver, converting incoming serial bits into parallel ASCII data and checking parity. Its inputs include the serial data line, shift, clear, load, final, count, clock, and enable signals; outputs are the 12-bit ASCII data, an end flag, a parity-OK indicator, and a 3-bit counter value. Internally, a shift register captures serial data, a 16-counter tracks bit positions, and a parity error detector validates the received word. The counter is cleared by the logical OR of the clear and zero inputs, while the end flag and ASCII data are routed directly from internal blocks.

A top-level CPU that sequences fetch/execute cycles using an internally divided clock and an external bus/RAM. Inputs are clk, reset, bus_ready, bus_parity, and read_mode; outputs include hlt_out, clk_out, a_data, RAM address/write-enable, and bus control/status/chip-select lines, with bidirectional ram_data and bus_data. Internally, a control unit drives an ALU, program counter, memory-address register, adder, and I/O mapping block. Multiplexers select PC or memory address for RAM and increment or jump target for the PC; a halt flag is latched until reset.

This module implements a two-input logical OR gate. It has two 1-bit input ports, x and y, and one 1-bit output port, z. Internally, a continuous assignment drives z with the bitwise OR of x and y. The output is purely combinational, with no clock, reset, or stored state. The output is high whenever either input is high.

This module is a start/stop-gated counter controlled by a small FSM. Its inputs are a clock, active-low reset, start, and stop; it has no outputs. The FSM has four states (init, loading, enabled, finished) that load a configurable length into an internal Counter and enable counting while start is asserted or stop is not. Counting ends when the Counter's done signal asserts, disabling the counter. Note the reset is listed as edge-sensitive yet tested as a low level, an unusual implementation.

This module is a 4-bit hexadecimal-to-seven-segment decoder/driver. It takes a clock, an enable, and a 4-bit hex input, and produces a 7-bit segment control output (bit 0 = segment a through bit 6 = segment g). A combinational case statement maps hex values 0–F to active-high segment patterns. The output is clock-modulated: when enabled, segments that should be lit use inverted clock polarity while unlit segments follow the clock; when disabled, all segments follow the clock.

ClockManager generates a registered output, CLK_gol, based on a video sync and button inputs. Its inputs are CLK, CLK_btn_fast, CLK_btn_once, and V_sync; CLK_gol is the only output. An internal 32-bit counter A increments when V_sync and CLK_btn_fast are both high. When V_sync is low and A exceeds 10, A resets and CLK_gol is asserted; otherwise CLK_gol is deasserted. The block is edge-triggered by V_sync, the buttons, CLK, and changes on A, though CLK and CLK_btn_once do not affect the logic.

This module performs a combinational 32-bit logical left shift by two bit positions, effectively multiplying the input by four. It has one 32-bit input, IN_A, and one 32-bit output, OUT_A. The output is continuously assigned the input shifted left by two, with the two most significant bits discarded.

This module implements a 32-bit 2-to-1 multiplexer. It has a single-bit select input, two 32-bit data inputs, and one 32-bit output. When the select is low, the output is driven by the first data input; when high, it is driven by the second. The logic is purely combinational, with no clock or state.

This module implements the DES round f-function, transforming a 32-bit half-block using a 48-bit round key. It takes inputs clk, 32-bit r_in, and 48-bit k_in, and produces 32-bit r_out. Internally, r_in is expanded to 48 bits and XORed with k_in, then split into eight 6-bit groups. Four clocked dual S-box instances map these groups into eight 4-bit values. The resulting 32-bit S-box output is bit-permuted to form r_out.
Response:
module f_fun(
input wire clk,
input wire [31:0] r_in,
input wire [47:0] k_in,
output wire [31:0] r_out
);
wire [47:0] blk_exp_s;
wire [47:0] post_exp_key_add_s;
wire [31:0] post_s_box_s;
  // E
  assign blk_exp_s = {r_in[0],r_in[31],r_in[30],r_in[29],r_in[28],r_in[27],r_in[28],r_in[27],r_in[26],r_in[25],r_in[24],r_in[23],r_in[24],r_in[23],r_in[22],r_in[21],r_in[20],r_in[19],r_in[20],r_in[19],r_in[18],r_in[17],r_in[16],r_in[15],r_in[16],r_in[15],r_in[14],r_in[13],r_in[12],r_in[11],r_in[12],r_in[11],r_in[10],r_in[9],r_in[8],r_in[7],r_in[8],r_in[7],r_in[6],r_in[5],r_in[4],r_in[3],r_in[4],r_in[3],r_in[2],r_in[1],r_in[0],r_in[31]};
  assign post_exp_key_add_s = blk_exp_s ^ k_in;
  s_box_l_dual_dram S_BOX_0(
      post_exp_key_add_s[47:42],
    {broken{0}},
    post_exp_key_add_s[41:36],
    clk,
    1'b0,
    post_s_box_s[31:28],
    post_s_box_s[27:24]);
  s_box_l_dual_dram S_BOX_1(
      post_exp_key_add_s[35:30],
    {broken{0}},
    post_exp_key_add_s[29:24],
    clk,
    1'b0,
    post_s_box_s[23:20],
    post_s_box_s[19:16]);
  s_box_l_dual_dram S_BOX_2(
      post_exp_key_add_s[23:18],
    {broken{0}},
    post_exp_key_add_s[17:12],
    clk,
    1'b0,
    post_s_box_s[15:12],
    post_s_box_s[11:8]);
  s_box_l_dual_dram S_BOX_3(
      post_exp_key_add_s[11:6],
    {broken{0}},
    post_exp_key_add_s[5:0],
    clk,
    1'b0,
    post_s_box_s[7:4],
    post_s_box_s[3:0]);
  assign r_out = {post_s_box_s[16],post_s_box_s[25],post_s_box_s[12],post_s_box_s[11],post_s_box_s[3],post_s_box_s[20],post_s_box_s[4],post_s_box_s[15],post_s_box_s[31],post_s_box_s[17],post_s_box_s[9],post_s_box_s[6],post_s_box_s[27],post_s_box_s[14],post_s_box_s[1],post_s_box_s[22],post_s_box_s[30],post_s_box_s[24],post_s_box_s[8],post_s_box_s[18],post_s_box_s[0],post_s_box_s[5],post_s_box_s[29],post_s_box_s[23],post_s_box_s[13],post_s_box_s[19],post_s_box_s[2],post_s_box_s[26],post_s_box_s[10],post_s_box_s[21],post_s_box_s[28],post_s_box_s[7]};
endmodule

Instruction: This module implements a 1-bit full adder that also exposes carry propagate and generate signals. It takes operand bits x and y plus carry-in cin, and produces sum z, carry-out cout, propagate p, and generate g. Internally, generate is x AND y, and propagate is x XOR y. The sum is the XOR of x, y, and cin, while carry-out is generate OR (propagate AND cin).

This module implements a level-sensitive D latch with an asynchronous active-high preset. Its inputs are D (data), E (enable), and PRE (preset), with Q as the latched output. When PRE is high, the internal state is forced to 1 with highest priority. Otherwise, while E is high, Q follows D; when E is low, Q holds its previous value. The output Q directly reflects the internal state.

This module implements a Moore finite-state machine that turns a push-button signal into a latched run/stop output. Inputs are clock, asynchronous active-high reset, and botao; output estado is high while running. Four states (PARADO, INICIANDO, CONTANDO, PARANDO) form a handshake/debounce sequence: a press advances from stopped to counting, and a release returns it to stopped. State memory updates on clock edges or reset, next-state logic depends on botao and current state, and output logic asserts estado only in INICIANDO or CONTANDO.
Response:
module start_stop(
input wire clock,
input wire reset,
input wire botao,
output reg estado
);
parameter [1:0]
  PARADO = 0,
  INICIANDO = 1,
  CONTANDO = 2,
  PARANDO = 3;
  // estados
reg [1:0] Eatual; reg [1:0] Eprox;  // proximo estado
  always @(posedge CLOCK, posedge reset) begin : P2
  // memoria de estado
    if(reset == 1'b1) begin
      Eatual <= PARADO;
    end else begin
      Eatual <= Eprox;
    end
  end
  always @(botao, Eatual) begin : P1
  // logica de proximo estado
    case(Eatual)
    PARADO : begin
      if(botao == 1'b0) begin
        Eprox <= PARADO;
      end
      else begin
        Eprox <= INICIANDO;
      end
    end
    INICIANDO : begin
      if(botao == 1'b1) begin
        Eprox <= INICIANDO;
      end
      else begin
        Eprox <= CONTANDO;
      end
    end
    CONTANDO : begin
      if(botao == 1'b0) begin
        Eprox <= CONTANDO;
      end
      else begin
        Eprox <= PARANDO;
      end
    end
    PARANDO : begin
      if(botao == 1'b1) begin
        Eprox <= PARANDO;
      end
      else begin
        Eprox <= PARADO;
      end
    end
    default : begin
      Eprox <= PARADO;
    end
    endcase
  end
  always @(*) begin
    case(Eatual)
  // logica de saida (Moore)
      INICIANDO,CONTANDO : estado <= 1'b1;
      default : estado <= 1'b0;
    endcase
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module is a finite-state-machine control path that generates a 37-bit control word, T. Its inputs are start, clk, and reset; its outputs are complete and T[0:36]. An 8-state registered FSM (init, S0–S5, done) advances from init to S0 when start is asserted, then steps through S0–S5 before returning to init. Reset forces init, and done asserts complete. Combinational output logic clears T each state and sets state-specific control bits, with T[36:0].

This module is a top-level wrapper that exposes a number-guessing game on an FPGA board. Its inputs are an 8-bit switch value and three push-buttons used to set, reveal, and submit a guess. It drives four seven-segment displays. Internally, it instantiates the game logic, connecting the switches and buttons, and routes the game's two display outputs to HEX0 and HEX1. HEX2 and HEX3 are forced off, keeping them blank.

This module implements a two-input exclusive-NOR (XNOR) logic gate. It has two 1-bit inputs, Anx and Bnx, and one 1-bit output, Ynx. The output is the logical complement of the exclusive-OR of the inputs, so Ynx is high when the two inputs are equal and low when they differ. Functionally, it acts as an equality detector for two single-bit signals.

This module implements a single-bit logical inverter. It has one input, `a`, and one output, `b`. Internally, the output is driven as the Boolean complement of the input. Therefore, `b` is high when `a` is low, and low when `a` is high. It is purely combinational and has no clock or stored state.

This module is a clock frequency synthesizer that converts a 32 MHz input clock into a 40 MHz output using a Xilinx DCM_SP. It has one clock input, CLKIN_IN, and three clock outputs: the synthesized clock CLKFX_OUT, a buffered copy of the input clock CLKIN_IBUFG_OUT, and CLK0_OUT. Internally, an IBUFG buffers the input into the DCM, which is configured to multiply by 5 and divide by 4. BUFG primitives drive the DCM feedback path and the synthesized clock output.
Response:
module dcm32to40(
input wire CLKIN_IN,
output wire CLKFX_OUT,
output wire CLKIN_IBUFG_OUT,
output wire CLK0_OUT
);
wire CLKFB_IN;
wire CLKFX_BUF;
wire CLKIN_IBUFG;
wire CLK0_BUF;
wire GND_BIT;
  assign GND_BIT = 1'b0;
  assign CLKIN_IBUFG_OUT = CLKIN_IBUFG;
  assign CLK0_OUT = CLKFB_IN;
  BUFG CLKFX_BUFG_INST(
      .I(CLKFX_BUF),
    .O(CLKFX_OUT));
  IBUFG CLKIN_IBUFG_INST(
      .I(CLKIN_IN),
    .O(CLKIN_IBUFG));
  BUFG CLK0_BUFG_INST(
      .I(CLK0_BUF),
    .O(CLKFB_IN));
  DCM_SP #(
      .CLK_FEEDBACK(2'b1X),
    .CLKDV_DIVIDE(2.0),
    .CLKFX_DIVIDE(4),
    .CLKFX_MULTIPLY(5),
    .CLKIN_DIVIDE_BY_2(FALSE),
    .CLKIN_PERIOD(31.250),
    .CLKOUT_PHASE_SHIFT(4'bNONE),
    .DESKEW_ADJUST(18'bSYSTEM_SYNCHRONOUS),
    .DFS_FREQUENCY_MODE(3'bLOW),
    .DLL_FREQUENCY_MODE(3'bLOW),
    .DUTY_CYCLE_CORRECTION(TRUE),
    .FACTORY_JF(16'hC080),
    .PHASE_SHIFT(0),
    .STARTUP_WAIT(FALSE))
  DCM_SP_INST(
      .CLKFB(CLKFB_IN),
    .CLKIN(CLKIN_IBUFG),
    .DSSEN(GND_BIT),
    .PSCLK(GND_BIT),
    .PSEN(GND_BIT),
    .PSINCDEC(GND_BIT),
    .RST(GND_BIT),
    .CLKDV(/* open */),
    .CLKFX(CLKFX_BUF),
    .CLKFX180(/* open */),
    .CLK0(CLK0_BUF),
    .CLK2X(/* open */),
    .CLK2X180(/* open */),
    .CLK90(/* open */),
    .CLK180(/* open */),
    .CLK270(/* open */),
    .LOCKED(/* open */),
    .PSDONE(/* open */),
    .STATUS(/* open */));
endmodule

Instruction: This module implements a two-input exclusive-OR logic gate. It has two 1-bit inputs, A and B, and one 1-bit output, C. The output is driven continuously by the logical XOR of the two inputs. Therefore, C is high only when A and B differ. When both inputs are equal, C is low.

This module generates synchronized global clock outputs from an external clock using a Xilinx DCM and global buffers. Inputs are CLKIN_IN, the source clock, and RST_IN, which resets the DCM. Outputs are CLKIN_IBUFG_OUT (buffered input clock), CLK0_OUT (zero-degree feedback clock), and CLKDV_OUT (divided clock). Internally, the input is buffered and fed to the DCM; its CLK0 output feeds back through a global buffer, and its divided output is buffered. The DCM is configured for divide-by-2 divided output, low-frequency mode, with unused controls tied low or left open.
Response:
module global_clock(
input wire CLKIN_IN,
input wire RST_IN,
output wire CLKDV_OUT,
output wire CLKIN_IBUFG_OUT,
output wire CLK0_OUT
);
wire CLKDV_BUF;
wire CLKFB_IN;
wire CLKIN_IBUFG;
wire CLK0_BUF;
wire GND_BIT;
  assign GND_BIT = 1'b0;
  assign CLKIN_IBUFG_OUT = CLKIN_IBUFG;
  assign CLK0_OUT = CLKFB_IN;
  BUFG CLKDV_BUFG_INST(
      .I(CLKDV_BUF),
    .O(CLKDV_OUT));
  IBUFG CLKIN_IBUFG_INST(
      .I(CLKIN_IN),
    .O(CLKIN_IBUFG));
  BUFG CLK0_BUFG_INST(
      .I(CLK0_BUF),
    .O(CLKFB_IN));
  DCM_SP #(
      .CLK_FEEDBACK(2'b1X),
    .CLKDV_DIVIDE(2.0),
    .CLKFX_DIVIDE(1),
    .CLKFX_MULTIPLY(4),
    .CLKIN_DIVIDE_BY_2(FALSE),
    .CLKIN_PERIOD(20.000),
    .CLKOUT_PHASE_SHIFT(4'bNONE),
    .DESKEW_ADJUST(18'bSYSTEM_SYNCHRONOUS),
    .DFS_FREQUENCY_MODE(3'bLOW),
    .DLL_FREQUENCY_MODE(3'bLOW),
    .DUTY_CYCLE_CORRECTION(TRUE),
    .FACTORY_JF(16'hC080),
    .PHASE_SHIFT(0),
    .STARTUP_WAIT(FALSE))
  DCM_SP_INST(
      .CLKFB(CLKFB_IN),
    .CLKIN(CLKIN_IBUFG),
    .DSSEN(GND_BIT),
    .PSCLK(GND_BIT),
    .PSEN(GND_BIT),
    .PSINCDEC(GND_BIT),
    .RST(RST_IN),
    .CLKDV(CLKDV_BUF),
    .CLKFX(/* open */),
    .CLKFX180(/* open */),
    .CLK0(CLK0_BUF),
    .CLK2X(/* open */),
    .CLK2X180(/* open */),
    .CLK90(/* open */),
    .CLK180(/* open */),
    .CLK270(/* open */),
    .LOCKED(/* open */),
    .PSDONE(/* open */),
    .STATUS(/* open */));
endmodule

Instruction: This combinational module converts a 16-bit RGB565 pixel into a 24-bit RGB888 pixel. It takes `rgb_565[15:0]` as input and drives `rgb_888[23:0]` as a registered output. The input is split into 5-bit red, 6-bit green, and 5-bit blue fields, each extended to 8 bits by left-shifting and OR-ing with a right-shifted copy. Note: the blue path ORs the left-shifted value with itself, so its low bits are effectively zero-filled.

This module is a PS/2 receive controller that deserializes incoming PS/2 data and validates parity. Its inputs are CLK, RST, PS2C (PS/2 clock), and PS2D (PS/2 serial data); outputs are the 8-bit PS2RX_DATA and PS2RX_VALID flag. A falling-edge detector on PS2C triggers a three-state FSM (idle, data, load) and a 4-bit bit counter. The counter shifts the eight data bits in LSB-first, captures the parity bit, then checks parity; PS2RX_VALID is asserted only when parity is correct.

This module is a MIPS-style main control unit that decodes a 6-bit opcode into datapath control signals. Its single input is the 6-bit Opcode; its outputs are the 1-bit signals RegDst, Branch, MemRead, MemtoReg, MemWrite, ALUSrc, RegWrite, and Jump, plus the 2-bit ALUOp. Combinational logic in an always block uses a case statement to recognize five instructions: R-type (add/sub), lw, beq, j, and sw, assigning a fixed control pattern for each. Unrecognized opcodes fall through the default branch, leaving outputs unchanged.

This module is a clock prescaler that generates a periodic enable pulse from a faster input clock. Its ports are CLK (input clock), CE (clock enable), CLR (asynchronous clear), and CEO (divided enable output). A 28-bit internal divider counts CLK edges only when CE is high, resetting to zero on CLR or after reaching divide_factor−1. The parameter divide_factor sets the division ratio, defaulting to 1,000,000, and CEO is asserted only when the counter reaches that terminal value while CE is high.
Response:
module Prescaler(
input wire CLK,
input wire CE,
input wire CLR,
output wire CEO
);
reg [27:0] DIVIDER;  // internal divider register 
parameter divide_factor = 1000000;  // divide factor user constant
// remember to adjust lenght of DIVIDER register when divide_factor is being changed
  always @(posedge CLK, posedge CLR) begin
    if(CLR == 1'b1) begin
      DIVIDER <= {28{1'b0}};
    end else begin
      if(CE == 1'b1) begin
        if(DIVIDER == (divide_factor - 1)) begin
          DIVIDER <= {28{1'b0}};
        end
        else begin
          DIVIDER <= DIVIDER + 1;
        end
      end
    end
  end
  assign CEO = DIVIDER == (divide_factor - 1) && CE == 1'b1 ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;
endmodule

Instruction:
This module acts as a keyboard matrix decoder that selects and outputs a 3-bit key-row value based on a 4-bit position input.

Its ports are a 25-bit active-low key input `keys_n`, a 4-bit `position` selector, and outputs `k_reset_n`, `k_int_n`, and `k_row`.

Combinational logic maps `keys_n[24]` directly to `k_reset_n` and `keys_n[19]` to `k_int_n`, while a case statement on `position` assembles `k_row` from selected key bits, defaulting to `3'b111` for unused positions.

This combinational controller decodes a 3-bit opcode into program-counter and stack control signals. Its input is opcode[2:0], and its outputs are stack_push, inc_select, stack_clk_enable, and 2-bit pc_value_select. Each valid opcode selects an operation: increment PC by 4, load PC from a value, increment PC by a value, push then load/increment PC, or pop from the stack. stack_push and stack_clk_enable reflect whether a stack push or pop is needed. Invalid opcodes default all outputs to zero.

This module performs one round of the DES Feistel cipher. It takes a clock, 32-bit left and right data halves, and a 48-bit round subkey, producing updated 32-bit halves. Internally it instantiates a clocked F-function submodule that combines the right half with the subkey. The new left output is the old right half, while the new right output is the old left half XORed with the F-function result.

This module converts a 4-bit Gray-coded input into its equivalent 4-bit binary value. It has a 4-bit input `gray` and a 4-bit output `bin`. Internally, a combinational always block derives the result: the most significant binary bit equals the Gray MSB, and each lower binary bit is formed by XORing the corresponding Gray bit with the binary bit immediately above it. The output continuously reflects this calculation.

This module implements a two-input logical OR gate. It has two 1-bit input ports, a and b, and one 1-bit output port, z. Internally, it continuously drives z to the logical OR of a and b. Therefore, z is high whenever either input is high, and low only when both inputs are low. The design is purely combinational.

This module is a logic analyzer: it samples a 32-bit input into block RAM and streams captured data over a UART serial link. Ports include reset, crystal clock, external sample clock, a 32-bit input, serial rx/tx (tx bidirectional), an 8-bit LED output, and switches. Internally a clock manager and debouncer condition clocks/reset, a UART block handles commands and data, a core executes commands with memory read/write control, and a block RAM stores samples. A free-running counter supplies the core's sample input, and the LEDs indicate clock, reset, switch, and serial-pin status.

This module implements a free-running binary counter that drives an 8-bit LED output, effectively acting as a clock divider. It has a single clock input and an 8-bit output bus for the LED indicators. Internally, a 26-bit tick register increments on every rising clock edge. The LED outputs are taken from the upper eight counter bits, so they toggle much more slowly than the input clock. There is no reset or enable control.

BRAM_S36_S144 is a dual-port block RAM wrapper exposing a 36-bit-wide port A and a 144-bit-wide port B, implemented with two parallel BRAM_S18_S72 primitives. Port A has an 11-bit address, 32 data plus 4 parity inputs, and outputs; port B has a 9-bit address, 128 data plus 16 parity inputs, and outputs. Both ports share independent clocks, write enables, enables, and set/reset signals. Internally, wide data and parity words are split into even and odd halves for the two primitives, then read data is re-interleaved into the full-width outputs.

This module is a parameterized digital delay line that shifts a serial input through a register chain and outputs the delayed bit. Its ports are an asynchronous reset `rst`, clock `clk`, serial data input `din`, and delayed serial output `dout`. Internally, a `DELAYLEN`-bit shift register captures `din` on each rising clock edge and shifts toward the output. The output is taken from the last register bit, so `dout` is `din` delayed by `DELAYLEN` cycles. Reset is active at the level selected by `RSTDEF` (default low) and clears the shift register.

The module implements an 8-input programmable interrupt controller that arbitrates interrupt requests by fixed priority and supplies the winning device identifier to a bus master.

Its ports include a clock, eight interrupt request inputs (IRQ_in), a one-hot interrupt acknowledge output (IAK_out) with a matching acknowledge input (IAK_in), a combined interrupt request output (IRQ_out), a chip-select/write-enable bus interface with 32-bit data in/out (CS, RW, Din, Dout), and unused-type/ready signals (DTYPE, RDY).

Two internal enable registers form a master enable latch: software writes toggled via CS and Din[0] enable or disable the controller, and the two registers must agree before interrupt handling proceeds.

When enabled and IAK_in is asserted, the logic latches the index of the highest-priority active IRQ input into an internal device register, drives the corresponding one-hot bit on IAK_out, and clears IRQ_out; otherwise IAK_out is cleared and IRQ_out reflects whether any request is pending.

Bus reads with CS asserted return the stored device index, while unselected accesses drive Dout to zero.

cmp_792 is a purely combinational 32-bit equality comparator. It has two 32-bit inputs, in1 and in0, and one 1-bit output, eq. Internally it compares the two input words and drives eq high when they are equal, and low otherwise. There is no clock, reset, or stored state.

This module is meant to derive a slower clock from an input clock, but it effectively holds its output low. It has a single input, clk_in, and a single output, clk_out. Internally, a 4-bit counter and an output register are updated on every rising edge of clk_in. Since the counter is only 4 bits wide, it can never reach the value 20 used in the toggle condition, so it just wraps around and the output never toggles.

car_core is a top-level audio/control core that bridges an I2S codec, an SPI host, and an LVDS link. Its ports include main_clk, reset, seq_reset, I2S clocks/data/word-select, SPI signals, FM mic sync, mute, and test outputs, with lvds_io as a bidirectional line. Internally it instantiates a car_sequencer for LVDS/SPI/I2S control and an i2s_dio_2 for I2S serialization/deserialization. A small register samples i2s_ws on the falling edge of main_clk to avoid a race and drives test_lrst_pre; SPI chip selects are inverted and spi_miso is tri-stated when neither is active.

A clocked blink-pattern generator with asynchronous reset. Its inputs are a 7-bit `binIn`, `clk`, and `reset`; outputs are a 7-bit `binOut` and a single-bit `outLed`. Reset clears a stored previous-input register and a counter. When `binIn` changes, the counter resets and the previous value updates; otherwise the counter cycles 0–6, alternating `binOut` between `binIn` and all-ones, then holds all-ones. A special one-shot occurs when `binIn` leaves 7'b1100011, driving `outLed` low and counting 7–13 to alternate all-ones with 1111110.

WBOPRT08 is a Wishbone slave that implements an 8-bit output port register. Its inputs are CLK_I, RST_I, STB_I, WE_I, and DAT_I[7:0]; its outputs are ACK_O, DAT_O[7:0], and the separate port output PRT_O[7:0]. On each rising clock edge, the internal register Q is cleared when RST_I is high, captures DAT_I when both STB_I and WE_I are asserted, and otherwise holds its current value. ACK_O directly follows STB_I, while DAT_O and PRT_O both continuously reflect Q.

BasedeTiempo2 is a clocked time-base generator meant to emit a one-clock reset pulse after a fixed count. Its ports are clock clk, asynchronous reset input rst_in, and registered output rst_out. A 4-bit state register P_S increments each clock; combinatorial logic sets N_S=P_S+1 and rst_out low, except at a terminal count where the state clears and rst_out goes high. P_S loads on the rising clk edge, or is cleared asynchronously by rst_in. The terminal-count constant is wider than the 4-bit state, so as written the pulse never occurs.

This module selects between two pairs of data inputs and registers the results, producing two synchronized outputs. Its inputs are two data pairs (A1/B1 and A2/B2), two select lines, a clock, and an active-low reset; outputs are Q1 and Q2. Each data pair feeds a 2:1 multiplexer controlled by its corresponding select line. The two mux outputs are captured on each rising clock edge by flip-flops, which asynchronously clear to zero while reset is low.

This module implements a combinational hexadecimal-to-seven-segment display decoder. It has a 4-bit input selecting a hex digit from 0 to F and a 7-bit output providing the corresponding segment pattern. Internally, a case statement maps each 4-bit value to a 7-bit pattern held in a combinational register, with a default pattern for unmatched values. The stored pattern is continuously assigned to the output port.

This module has no inputs and one 8-bit output, `val`. It continuously drives that output to a fixed 8-bit constant pattern. The most significant bit is high-impedance, the next six bits are 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, and the least significant bit is unknown. There is no clocked or other internal logic.

This module implements a simple two-input AND gate. It has two single-bit inputs, a and b, and one single-bit output, c. Internally, the output is assigned the logical AND of the two inputs. Thus, c is high only when both a and b are high; otherwise, c is low.

Combinational module that generates pixel colours for a simple obstacle game frame. Inputs are the player row, obstacle low/high extents and position, pixel row and column, and enable; outputs are a 3-bit colour and a 32-bit obstacle ID. Background defaults to black, while the player pixel is magenta. The obstacle index is the column divided by the per-obstacle band width; a green obstacle is drawn in that band at a column offset by obst_pos whenever the row lies above obst_high or below V_RES-1-obst_low. Outputs are high-Z/zero when enable is low.

This module implements a clocked finite-state machine that advances through the sequence 000, 010, 101, 110, then back to 000 when enabled. It has a 3-bit input `entrada`, asynchronous reset, enable, clock, and a registered 3-bit output `saida`. An internal register holds the state; reset clears it, and while enable is high the next state is selected from `entrada`, otherwise it holds. Because `saida` loads from this register on each non-reset clock edge, it reflects the previous state, and reset only clears the internal register.

This module provides synchronous instruction-dispatch control. It takes a clock, a 4-bit opcode, and three 4-bit register addresses (RA, RB, RA4), producing registered outputs IMM_SEL, DC1, and DC2. On each rising edge, IMM_SEL is set based on the opcode, selecting immediate when the opcode is 5–10 and otherwise clearing it. DC1 is asserted when RA matches RA4, and DC2 when RB matches RA4.

This module drives two RGB LEDs with smoothly cycling colors. It has one clock input, GCLK, and two 3-bit outputs, RGB_LED_1_O and RGB_LED_2_O. Internally, counters generate a fast PWM window and a slower color step; from the step counter it derives increment/decrement ramps and selects red, green, blue intensities by phase. Each intensity is compared with the PWM window to set one output bit, so both LEDs show the same PWM-modulated color pattern.

This module implements a single D flip-flop with an intended active-low asynchronous reset. Its ports are the clock `i_Clock`, reset `i_Reset_n`, data input `i_D`, and registered output `o_Q`. In an always block, `Q` is cleared to 0 when `i_Reset_n` is low, otherwise it captures `i_D` on the clock edge; `o_Q` is continuously assigned from `Q`. Note the reset sensitivity uses `posedge i_Reset_n` rather than `negedge`, which is likely a bug.

This module is an unsigned leading-one detector (priority encoder) for a 36-bit fraction. It takes input `frac[36:1]` and produces a 6-bit one-hot output `count[6:1]` marking the position of the most significant set bit. The input is split into six 6-bit groups, and group-level OR terms (`sec`) plus `sel` identify the first non-empty group. Six `hcc_usgnpos` submodules compute each group's position with appropriate start offsets, and the selected group's position is multiplexed onto `count`.

This top-level module is a board wrapper that connects FPGA board I/O to a system_controller instance. Its inputs are a 50 MHz clock, four keys, 5-bit row select, and bidirectional 16-bit SRAM data; outputs drive LEDs, SRAM address/control, keypad columns, an LCD, and eight seven-segment displays. It permanently enables the LCD and forces HEX6/HEX7 off. All remaining SRAM, keypad, LCD, and display signals route to system_controller, using KEY[0] as reset and LEDG[0] to report program mode.
Response:
module top_level(
input wire CLOCK_50,
input wire [3:0] KEY,
output wire [7:0] LEDG,
output wire [17:0] SRAM_ADDR,
inout wire [15:0] SRAM_DQ,
output wire SRAM_WE_N,
output wire SRAM_OE_N,
output wire SRAM_UB_N,
output wire SRAM_LB_N,
output wire SRAM_CE_N,
input wire [4:0] ROW_SEL,
output wire [3:0] COL_SEL,
output wire [7:0] LCD_DATA,
output wire LCD_EN,
output wire LCD_RS,
output wire LCD_ON,
output wire [7:0] HEX0,
output wire [7:0] HEX1,
output wire [7:0] HEX2,
output wire [7:0] HEX3,
output wire [7:0] HEX4,
output wire [7:0] HEX5,
output wire [7:0] HEX6,
output wire [7:0] HEX7
);
  assign LCD_ON = 1'b1;
  assign HEX6 = 8'hFF;
  assign HEX7 = 8'hFF;
  system_controller Inst_system_controller(
      .clk_50(CLOCK_50),
    .reset_key(KEY[0]),
    .op_prog_mode(LEDG[0]),
    .sram_addr(SRAM_ADDR),
    .sram_dq(SRAM_DQ),
    .sram_we_n(SRAM_WE_N),
    .sram_oe_n(SRAM_OE_N),
    .sram_ub_n(SRAM_UB_N),
    .sram_lb_n(SRAM_LB_N),
    .sram_ce_n(SRAM_CE_N),
    .row_sel(ROW_SEL),
    .col_sel(COL_SEL),
    .lcd_data_out(LCD_DATA),
    .lcd_enable_out(LCD_EN),
    .lcd_select_out(LCD_RS),
    .hex0(HEX0),
    .hex1(HEX1),
    .hex2(HEX2),
    .hex3(HEX3),
    .hex4(HEX4),
    .hex5(HEX5));
endmodule

Instruction: The module generates an incrementing 8-bit LED pattern synchronized to the input clock. It has a clock input, clk, and an 8-bit registered output, LED_output. Internally, a 32-bit counter counts clock cycles until it reaches 5,000,000, then resets. On that event, an 8-bit pattern register increments and its value is driven onto LED_output, updating the displayed pattern every 5 million clock cycles.

Output_Port_MUX is a four-way, 32-bit output-port demultiplexer. It accepts clock, reset, enable, a 32-bit data word, and a 2-bit select, and drives four 32-bit registered outputs. Combinational decoding of sel, gated by enable, asserts exactly one of four register enable lines, so the selected output captures data on the falling clock edge while the others hold their values. Reset clears the output registers.

This module is a PWM LED driver that produces a brightness-controlled output. Inputs are clk, a 1 MHz tick, synchronous reset, an 8-bit brightness value, and an invert control; the only output is led. On each tick, an 8-bit counter increments; the internal LED signal goes high when the counter equals brightness and low when the counter wraps to zero. Reset clears the counter and turns the LED off, and the final led output is the internal signal XORed with invert.

This module generates a servo control pulse whose width is set by an 8-bit angle input. Inputs are Angulo, Clk, and Rst; the only output is Senal. A free-running counter, asynchronously cleared by Rst, counts clock cycles up to MaxCta before wrapping. The required pulse width is computed as 100000 plus Angulo times 392, and Senal stays high while the counter is below that value, producing a PWM-like signal proportional to the commanded angle.

This module implements a combinational 32-bit binary adder. It has two 32-bit inputs, A and B, and one 32-bit output, SumOut. Internally, SumOut is continuously assigned the arithmetic sum of A and B. Because the output is only 32 bits wide, any carry beyond bit 31 is discarded, and no carry or overflow signal is provided.

This module is a clocked finite-state controller that produces a write cycle for an external memory or peripheral. Inputs are clock, async reset, CPU write and chip-select requests, and parity; outputs are address-enable, write-enable, and write-strobe. A state register resets to idle and otherwise advances from combinational next-state logic. In idle, address-enable is high; after write, chip-select, and parity all go high, it steps through hold/load/strobe states, asserting write-enable only in the final write-data state and pulling write-strobe low during strobe.

This module implements a five-state controller FSM. It has inputs `clk` and asynchronous reset `rst`, and outputs `register_load` and `register_shift`. Reset forces the state to S0; otherwise it advances S0→S1→S2→S3→S4→S0 each clock. The state decoder asserts `register_load` in S0 and `register_shift` in S1, while both outputs hold their previous values in S2–S4 because they are not assigned there.

This module debounces a mechanical button by requiring the input to stay stable for a programmable number of clock cycles. Its ports are `clk`, `button`, and `result`. Two internal flip-flops synchronize and compare the button signal to detect changes. A counter is reset whenever a change is detected, and when the input remains stable long enough, the synchronized value is latched to the output. The `counter_size` parameter sets the counter width and therefore the debounce interval.

rc_counter is a 32-bit raster-scan counter producing column and row positions for a 2D grid. Its inputs are Clk, active-low reset RSTn, and enable En; outputs are ColPos and RowPos, with parameters num_cols and num_rows (each default 512) defining grid size. When enabled on a rising clock edge, the column counter increments; reaching num_cols resets it to zero and advances the row counter, which wraps to zero after num_rows. Reset is intended to clear both outputs. Note the sensitivity list also triggers on RSTn and En edges, which is nonstandard.

A clocked 24-bit-to-8-bit serializer that outputs a 24-bit word as three bytes in MSB-to-LSB order using ready/valid handshaking. Inputs: clk_in, active-high reset_in, 24-bit data24_in, and valid24_in; outputs: ready24_out, 8-bit data8_out, and valid8_out, throttled by ready8_in. A three-state FSM (MSB, MID, LSB) passes the MSB directly while capturing the middle and low bytes into registers. ready24_out is asserted only in the MSB state, and valid8_out only when ready8_in is high.

This module implements a two-input XNOR logic gate. It has two single-bit inputs, A and B, and one single-bit output, C. The output is high when A and B are equal, and low when they differ. Internally, it derives this by complementing the exclusive-OR result of the two inputs. The design is purely combinational, with no clock or stored state.

pos_loader sequentially captures three 16-bit coordinates (x, y, z) from an external data source using a request/ready handshake. Its inputs are clock, reset, enable, start, data_in, busy_ram, and RxRdy_ram; outputs are go_ram, RxRdy_out, and registered x/y/z. A state machine starts in IDLE on start when RAM is not busy, asserts go_ram, then waits for RxRdy_ram to latch each word into x, y, then z. After z, it pulses RxRdy_out and re-requests X while enabled; reset clears go_ram and returns to IDLE.

**Function:** This module composites a two-color pointer/sprite over a background pixel stream, outputting the blended pixel.

**Ports:** Inputs are CLK, PO (pointer enable), PS (sprite-bank select), X/Y (pointer position), ADDR (pixel address) and DIN (background pixel); DOUT is the composed pixel.

**Internal logic:** It derives relative x/y offsets and a ROM address, then reads black and white sprite mask bytes from two ROMs. A case on the low bits of X shifts these masks into 16-bit values to align the sprite, and the output logic blends DIN with the selected mask bytes when the pointer is within its sprite window, otherwise passing DIN through unchanged.

Module add_169 is a 27-bit adder that outputs the low 27 bits of the sum of its two inputs, effectively discarding any overflow beyond bit 26. It has a 27-bit output `result` and two 27-bit inputs, `in_a` and `in_b`. Internally, it shifts each input left by one bit, sets the first shifted value’s least significant bit to 1, and adds the two 29-bit values. The output is taken from bits 27 down to 1 of that sum, giving `in_a + in_b` modulo 2^27.

This module implements an 8-bit read-only memory (ROM) that asynchronously maps an 8-bit address to an 8-bit data value. Input `A` is the 8-bit address; output `D` is the registered 8-bit data word. A combinational `case` block translates addresses `0x00`–`0x17` and `0xFE`–`0xFF` into fixed constants, while all other addresses assign a don't-care value. The stored contents are currently placeholder/dummy values intended to be replaced later.

This module implements a 12-bit multiplexer controlled by an 8-bit select input. It has six 12-bit data inputs (i_0 through i_5) and one 12-bit registered output o. Internally, a case statement maps select values 0,1,2,3 to i_0,i_1,i_2,i_3 respectively. Select values 4 and 5 are not decoded, and the default branch assigns nothing, so o holds its previous value for other select codes. Because the always block is sensitive only to i_select, changes on data inputs alone do not update o.
Response:
module mux(
input wire [7:0] i_select,
input wire [11:0] i_0,
input wire [11:0] i_1,
input wire [11:0] i_2,
input wire [11:0] i_3,
input wire [11:0] i_4,
input wire [11:0] i_5,
output reg [11:0] o
);
  always @(i_select) begin
    case(i_select)
    8'h00 : begin
      o <= i_0;
    end
    8'h01 : begin
      o <= i_1;
    end
    8'h02 : begin
      o <= i_2;
    end
    8'h03 : begin
      o <= i_3;
    end
    default : begin
      // do nothing
    end
    endcase
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module generates simple VGA graphics from pixel coordinates, drawing an outer frame and a movable box. Its inputs are the pixel position VGA_X/VGA_Y, plus control signals TITLE, SCORE, and VISIBLE; its outputs are mapped map coordinates MAP_X/MAP_Y and 4-bit RGB color outputs. Internally, an XY2MAP submodule converts pixel coordinates into grid and box coordinates. The frame is enabled at fixed screen boundary rows and columns, while the box is enabled when the box coordinates are valid and VISIBLE is high. The RGB outputs are set to full white where either the frame or visible box is active, and black otherwise.

This module is a pipeline register that transfers instruction-fetch data from the IF stage to the ID stage. It accepts a clock, a 32-bit instruction, and a 32-bit PC+4 value as inputs, and provides registered versions of those two values as outputs. On each rising clock edge, the instruction and PC+4 inputs are captured and driven onto the outputs. It contains no combinational logic beyond these synchronous register updates.

T_REG is a one-bit register that captures T_in on the rising edge of clk and drives T_out. Its ports are clk, reset, T_in, and T_out, with T_out as the registered output. In the always block, if reset is low, T_out is cleared to 0; otherwise T_out is loaded with T_in. The block is also sensitive to a rising edge on reset, so the reset behavior is not a normal asynchronous clear; it effectively acts as an active-low synchronous clear on clock edges.
Response:
module T_REG(
input wire clk,
input wire reset,
input wire T_in,
output reg T_out
);
  always @(posedge reset, posedge clk) begin
    if((reset == 1'b0)) begin
      T_out <= 1'b0;
    end else begin
      T_out <= T_in;
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module partitions a 32-bit input value into three independently captured slices, each with its own clock and asynchronous control. Its inputs are three control/reset signals, three clocks, and the 32-bit value `ival`; there are no outputs. One 14-bit register resets high on `reset` and loads `ival[31:18]` on `sysclk` rising edges. A 3-bit register clears low on `preset` and loads `ival[2:0]` on `dsysclk` falling edges. Another 3-bit register clears low on `qreset` and loads `ival[6:4]` on `esysclk` falling edges.

This module is an SPI clock divider that generates the serial clock SCL and a transmit-enable strobe. Its inputs are `clk`, active-low `resetN`, `sclEnable`, and `sclSpeed`, while outputs are `scl` and `tsrEnable`. When enabled, an internal counter increments and is cleared at the selected slow or fast divider limit. Half-period comparisons toggle SCL and pulse `tsrEnable`, assuming SPI polarity and phase are zero.

This module implements a 32-bit ALU that decodes a 6-bit opcode to select an arithmetic or bitwise operation on two 32-bit operands. Its ports are inputs a, b, and opcode, plus clk (unused), and a 32-bit registered output result. Internally, a combinational case statement computes addition, subtraction, negation, absolute value, bitwise OR, AND, XOR, or complement. For unrecognized opcodes, result is driven to all-unknown (X).

This module provides a simple 32-bit memory interface built around an 8Kx32 block RAM, using a 13-bit internal address counter to sequence accesses. Its ports are a clock, 32-bit data input and output, plus read and write control signals. The input data is routed directly to the RAM, and the RAM output directly drives the module output. On each rising clock edge, a write increments the address, while a read decrements it; writes take priority if both are asserted, and neither leaves it unchanged.

This module is a PS/2 keyboard receiver that deserializes an 8-bit scancode from the keyboard's clock and data lines. Its inputs are the system clock, active-low reset, and PS/2 clock/data lines; outputs are the 8-bit keycode and a code-enable strobe. Internally, it synchronizes the PS/2 clock, detects its falling edge, and runs a state machine through start, eight data bits (LSB first), parity, and stop bit. Valid odd parity and a high stop bit complete the frame, latch the scancode into the keycode output, and assert code-enable; code-enable clears when the next start bit is detected.

This module detects a two-sample pattern on the keyboard clock and produces a single-bit flag. It takes inputs `kbclk`, `reset`, and `clk`, and outputs registered signal `rf`. A two-bit shift register stores recent `kbclk` samples, updating on rising edges of `kbclk`, `clk`, or `reset`. Asynchronous reset initializes the history to binary 11; otherwise the history shifts. The output `rf` is high only when the stored history equals binary 10, and low otherwise.

This module computes the 32-bit difference of two 32-bit inputs, functioning as a subtractor that outputs in_a minus in_b and ignores borrow/carry.

Ports are a 32-bit output result and two 32-bit inputs, in_a and in_b.

Internally, each operand is widened to 34 bits by padding a zero on both the high and low ends. The widened operands are subtracted, and the middle 32 bits of the 34-bit difference are driven to result, discarding the guard bits.

This module implements a 1-bit full adder, producing a sum and carry-out from two operand bits and a carry-in. Its inputs are in1, in2, and c_in; outputs are sum and c_out. Internally, sum is the parity of the three inputs, and carry-out is asserted when at least two inputs are high. The logic uses intermediate XOR and AND terms combined by an OR to form the final carry-out.

An 8×8 LED dot-matrix controller that scans rows and drives columns to display a fixed pattern. It has inputs SMCLK and RESET, and outputs 8-bit ROW and LED buses. A 5-bit counter divides SMCLK, producing an enable every 32 cycles. A 3-bit row counter advances on that enable; combinational logic decodes it into one-hot row selection and an active-low column pattern. RESET clears both counters.

This module is a 10-state finite state machine that acts as a modulo-10 counter, advancing one state per clock. It has an asynchronous active-high reset (rst) and a clock (clk), and produces an 8-bit registered output Q. A 4-bit state register cycles s0 through s9 on each clk rising edge and returns to s0 on a rst rising edge. A combinational decoder maps states to Q values 0–7, then 9 and 10, skipping 8.
Response:
module D2_C1(
input wire rst,
input wire clk,
output reg [7:0] Q
);
parameter [3:0]
  s0 = 0,
  s1 = 1,
  s2 = 2,
  s3 = 3,
  s4 = 4,
  s5 = 5,
  s6 = 6,
  s7 = 7,
  s8 = 8,
  s9 = 9;
reg [3:0] s;
  always @(posedge rst, posedge clk) begin
    if((rst == 1'b1)) begin
      s <= s0;
    end else begin
      case(s)
      s0 : begin
        s <= s1;
      end
      s1 : begin
        s <= s2;
      end
      s2 : begin
        s <= s3;
      end
      s3 : begin
        s <= s4;
      end
      s4 : begin
        s <= s5;
      end
      s5 : begin
        s <= s6;
      end
      s6 : begin
        s <= s7;
      end
      s7 : begin
        s <= s8;
      end
      s8 : begin
        s <= s9;
      end
      s9 : begin
        s <= s0;
      end
      endcase
    end
  end
  always @(s) begin
    case(s)
    s0 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000000;
    end
    s1 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000001;
    end
    s2 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000010;
    end
    s3 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000011;
    end
    s4 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000100;
    end
    s5 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000101;
    end
    s6 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000110;
    end
    s7 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00000111;
    end
    s8 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00001001;
    end
    s9 : begin
      Q <= 8'b00001010;
    end
    endcase
  end
// rst = 0.5Mhz, clk=10Mhz
endmodule

Instruction: A 32-bit barrel shifter that performs logical left, logical right, arithmetic right, or rotate right on its 32-bit data input, with the operation chosen by a 2-bit mode and the distance by a 5-bit shift amount. Outputs are the shifted 32-bit result and a carry flag that is high whenever the shift amount is nonzero. Internally it uses five cascaded stages that each conditionally shift by 1, 2, 4, 8, or 16 bits, enabled by the corresponding bit of the shift amount. The rotate path feeds shifted-out bits back in at the opposite end, while arithmetic right shift replicates the sign bit at the MSB.

This is an 8-bit shift register with an enable and an asynchronous, active-low reset. Its inputs are Reset, Clk, Enable, and serial data D, and its output Q is the current 8-bit register value. On a low Reset, the register clears to zero; otherwise, on each rising clock edge when Enable is high, the register shifts right and loads D into the most significant bit. When Enable is low, the register holds its current value, and Q continuously reflects the internal register contents. Note that the port names are capitalized while the body references lowercase clk, reset, and enable, which would need to match in a real synthesis.

This module is a 32-bit adder that adds a zero-extended 30-bit operand to a 32-bit operand. It takes a 30-bit first input, a 32-bit second input, and produces a 32-bit sum output. Internally, the 30-bit input is widened to 32 bits by setting its upper two bits to zero. This widened value is then added to the second input to generate the output.

This module implements a single-bit 2-to-1 multiplexer. It has three 1-bit inputs: A and B are the data inputs, and S is the select control; Z is the 1-bit output. Combinational logic drives Z to A when S is 0 and to B when S is 1.

This module is a clock controller that derives two slower clocks from a single input clock and selects one as its output. It has an input clock, a switch input sw0, and an output clk. Internally, two CDiv divider instances generate a 5 Hz and a 1 kHz clock using their respective terminal-count parameters. A multiplexer-like assignment then drives clk: it outputs the 1 kHz clock when sw0 is low and the 5 Hz clock when sw0 is high.

This module implements a combinational 1-bit half adder. It has two 1-bit inputs, `in_0` and `in_1`, and two 1-bit outputs, `sum` and `carry_out`. The `sum` output is the exclusive-OR of the two inputs. The `carry_out` output is the AND of the two inputs. It contains no sequential or state-holding logic.

The module `first` is a purely combinational 4-bit pass-through circuit. It has a 4-bit input bus, `btn`, and a 4-bit output bus, `led`. Internally, every output bit is directly connected to the corresponding input bit. Therefore, `led` always reflects the current value of `btn`. There is no clock, reset, or stored state.

This module is a 16-bit byte-addressable register slice that stores incoming byte data into a selected half of the register. Inputs are clk, active-low reset rst_n, a 1-bit address selecting which byte lane to write, 8-bit data, and a write-valid strobe; outputs are the 16-bit registered value and a continuously asserted read strobe. On each rising clock edge, if the valid signal is high, the byte selected by the address is replaced with the input data while the other byte is retained, and reset clears the whole register to zero. The output always reflects the current register contents.

This module implements a two-input logical OR gate. It has two 1-bit inputs, A and B, and one 1-bit output, R. The output is high whenever either input is high, and low only when both inputs are low. Its behavior is purely combinational, with no clocked or state-holding elements.

Combinational VGA tile decoder for a Minesweeper-style game. Inputs are a 2-bit game_state (win and game-over) and an 8-bit element describing a cell's flag, covered, mine, and number bits; output elemidx is a 6-bit index into a graphics ROM. Internally it derives win, end, covered, flagged, and mine flags, then uses a priority if-else chain to select the ROM index for a closed block, numbered block, explosion, flag, revealed mine, wrong flag, or error fallback.

This module acts as a single-bit buffer or feed-through. It has one input port, data_i, and one output port, data_o. The output continuously follows the input without inversion or storage. A parameter named WITH_GENERIC defaults to TRUE but does not affect operation. The module contains no other logic or state.

The module implements a 2-bit-wide three-input multiplexer. Its inputs are select lines S1 and S0 plus 2-bit data inputs U, V, and W; its output is the 2-bit result M. Internally, S1 high selects W, while S1 low selects U when S0 is low and V when S0 is high. The same selection logic is applied independently to both bits of the output bus.

This module synchronizes an asynchronous input signal into a clock domain, providing a parameterizable multi-stage synchronizer to reduce metastability. Its ports are an asynchronous reset input, a clock input, an asynchronous signal input, and the synchronized output. A parameter sets the number of synchronization stages (default two), and another sets the reset value. Internally, a shift register of that many stages samples the async input on each clock edge and drives the output from its last stage; the asynchronous reset loads all stages with the configured initial value.

This module implements an 8-bit unsigned adder. It has two 8-bit inputs, in_a and in_b, and one 8-bit output, result. Internally, it widens both operands to 10 bits, appends a fixed 1 to in_a and 0 to in_b, adds them, and takes the middle eight bits of the sum. This produces the low eight bits of in_a + in_b, effectively discarding any carry or overflow.

This module implements a 2-to-4 decoder with an enable. It takes a 2-bit select_line and an active-high en input, producing a 4-bit data output. An internal decoded value maps select_line values 00, 01, and 10 to one-hot patterns 0001, 0010, and 0100, while 11 maps to 1111. When en is low, data is forced to 0000; otherwise data follows the decoded value.

The `vhd_e` module implements a simple combinational two-input AND gate. It has two 1-bit inputs, `A` and `B`, and one 1-bit output, `C`. The output is continuously assigned the logical AND of the two inputs. Therefore, `C` is high only when both `A` and `B` are high; otherwise it is low.

This top module integrates an x86-style CPU, 40 KB SRAM, 256-byte bootstrap ROM, and 16550-compatible UART. Its inputs are a 40 MHz clock, reset PIN3, serial RXD, and UART CTS; outputs include TXD, RTS, CPU-error LED1, UART-driven LED2N/LED3N, and PIN4. The CPU drives an address/data bus; a multiplexer selects read data from UART, bootstrap ROM, or SRAM via chip-select decoding. UART is mapped to I/O 0x3F8–0x3FF and bootstrap ROM to 0xFFF00. Reset comes from PIN3, and modem status inputs are tied inactive.

The module implements a turn-signal LED animation driver. Inputs are clock `clk`, active-high reset, and enable `en`; output is 3-bit `led_out`. A six-state finite state machine cycles through LED patterns 000, 100, 110, 111, 011, 001, advancing every 6,250,000 clock cycles via an internal counter. Reset or `en` low clears the state and turns all LEDs off. After the last state it returns to the first, creating a repeating sweep with an off pause.

This module is a single-bit D flip-flop intended to include an active-low asynchronous reset. Its inputs are i_Clock, i_Reset_n, and i_D; its output o_Q is the registered value. Internally, reg Q updates on the rising edge of either i_Clock or i_Reset_n: if i_Reset_n is low, Q clears to zero, otherwise Q captures i_D. Note the reset is only evaluated on i_Reset_n’s rising edge, so it is not a true level-sensitive asynchronous clear.

This module is a PS/2 keyboard interface that detects presses of the W, S, A, D, and space keys. Its inputs are a system clock, synchronous reset, and the PS/2 clock and data lines; its outputs are single-cycle pulse signals for each detected key. Internally, it debounces the PS/2 clock, deserializes incoming PS/2 data, and decodes the received scan code. Each decoded code is compared against the expected scan codes for W, S, A, D, and space, and rising-edge detectors convert the match conditions into output pulses.

The WB module implements the write-back stage of a pipelined processor. It accepts clock, reset, 32-bit data_from_MEM, and a 6-bit cntl_from_ID control word, and outputs 32-bit rfile_write_data_to_ID plus 5-bit rfile_write_addr_to_ID and rfile_write_e_to_ID for register-file writes and forwarding. Internally, the memory data is captured in one 32-bit register, while the control word is delayed through three cascaded 6-bit registers to match that latency. The final control word's upper five bits give the write address and its lowest bit is the write enable. All registers share the clock and reset.

An 8-bit ALU whose registered outputs update on the falling edge of clk. Inputs are 8-bit operands A and B, a 3-bit operator select, and a carry-in; outputs are an 8-bit result plus carry, zero, sign, parity, and auxiliary-carry flags. Select bits [2:1] choose addition (with optional carry-in) or subtraction (with optional borrow), while 100/101/110 do bitwise AND/XOR/OR and 111 compares by subtracting.
