Flags derive from a 9-bit internal sum/difference: carry from its MSB, sign from bit 7, parity from an XOR reduction, zero when the value is zero; auxiliary carry stays cleared.

This module is a hex seven-segment decoder with ripple blanking. It takes a 4-bit code and RippleBlank_In, and outputs a 7-bit segment pattern and RippleBlank_Out. Combinational logic maps the concatenated blanking input and code to an 8-bit value; the MSB is RippleBlank_Out and the lower 7 bits drive segments. Valid codes 0–15 produce hex digits; the ripple-blank state blanks the display and propagates the blanking signal, while unused codes produce a default pattern.

The ms_timer module generates a 1-millisecond timing tick from a 32 MHz input clock. It has one input, clk, and one registered output, clk_1ms. Internally, a 22-bit counter increments on each rising clock edge until it reaches 31,999, then resets to zero. On that terminal count, clk_1ms is driven high for one clock cycle and remains low otherwise. Thus the output is a one-cycle-wide pulse repeating every 1 ms.

This module is a single-port synchronous RAM with 256 eight-bit words. It has a clock, an enable, an 8-bit data input, an 8-bit address, a write-enable, and an 8-bit data output. On each rising clock edge, when enabled, it either writes the input data to the addressed location or reads the stored word from that location. The read data is registered and appears on the output one cycle later.

This module is an ALU control decoder that translates a 3-bit ALU operation class and a 6-bit function field into a 2-bit ALU control signal. Its inputs are `funct` and `AluOp`; its registered output is `AluCtr`. The combinational `always` block reacts to either input and defaults `AluCtr` to 00. For R-type operations (`AluOp` = 010), `funct` selects add, subtract, AND, or OR; other `AluOp` values directly select subtract, add, AND, or OR, with add as the fallback.

This module is a UDP test sink that displays received UDP payload bytes on an LED output. Its inputs are a clock, receive-valid strobe, 8-bit received data, source IP and source port, a destination-broadcast flag, and a 16-bit destination port; the only output is an 8-bit LED register. On each rising clock edge, when the receive-valid signal is high and the destination port equals 4660 (0x1414), the received data byte is latched into the LEDs. The module also registers the previous receive-valid value for potential edge detection, though that stored bit is not otherwise used.

This module implements a simple two-input OR gate. It has two 1-bit inputs, A and B, and one 1-bit output, C. The output is driven combinationally to the logical OR of the two inputs. It contains no sequential state, clock, or reset logic.

**Function:** Converts a 12-bit binary value into four BCD digits using the double-dabble (shift-and-add-3) algorithm.

**Ports:** Input `binIN` (12 bits); registered 4-bit outputs `ones`, `tens`, `hundreds`, `thousands`.

**Internal logic:** Whenever `binIN` changes, a 16-bit accumulator is cleared and 12 iterations run: each BCD nibble greater than 4 has 3 added, then the accumulator and a temporary copy of the input are shifted left together, feeding in one input bit per cycle. After 12 shifts, the accumulator's four nibbles are latched to the outputs.

This module is a four-state finite-state machine controlling a game's display, LEDs, and timing. Inputs are clock, active-low reset, and control signals ENTER, TARGET, END_TIME, and END_BONUS; outputs are state code STATESS, display select SEL_DISP, LED select, roll setup, timer enable, and reset. A clocked process updates the current state, while a combinational process assigns state-dependent outputs and selects the next state. States sequence through initialization, setup, active game, and end, with ENTER advancing most states and TARGET, END_TIME, or END_BONUS terminating play.

alu32 is a 32-bit ALU performing arithmetic, logic, comparison, and shift operations selected by a 4-bit control input. Its inputs are the 32-bit operands ia and ib, a 5-bit shift amount shamt, shift direction shdir, and control; outputs are the 32-bit result plus carry C, zero Z, sign S, and overflow V flags. Internally, 32 chained one-bit ALU slices compute arithmetic/logic and less-than results and carry, a shifter produces shifted data, and a multiplexer selects between them. Flags come from the result and the two most significant carries.

This module is a single-bit combinational AND gate. It has two inputs, Branch and IN_A, and one output, OUT_A. The output is high only when both inputs are high; otherwise it is low. It contains no sequential logic or state.

This module computes a single-bit parity-based output from nine 2-bit input symbols. Its ports are clock, reset, nine 2-bit inputs (single0–single8), and a one-bit output player. Each 2-bit input has its two bits XORed together, then those nine results are XORed to form player, making it the overall parity of all 18 input bits. Clock and reset do not affect the logic.

This module implements a two-input exclusive-OR (XOR) logic gate. It has two 1-bit input ports, x and y, and one 1-bit output port, z. The output is combinational, continuously assigned to the XOR of the two inputs. Thus z is high only when x and y differ, and low when both inputs are equal.

divisor2 is a programmable clock divider that produces a slower output clock from an input clock, with the division ratio selected by two speed inputs. Its ports are reset and clk inputs, velocidad0 and velocidad1 select inputs, and reloj output. Internally, a 25-bit counter increments on each rising clk edge, and an auxiliary flip-flop toggles when the counter reaches a terminal value determined by velocidad0 and velocidad1. The counter is cleared on reset or after each toggle, yielding a 50% duty-cycle divided clock.

This module is a bus builder that concatenates three individual 1-bit input signals into a single 3-bit output bus. It has one 3-bit output and three 1-bit inputs, named in0, in1, and in2. A width parameter defaults to 3. Internally, each output bit is directly driven by its corresponding input: output bit 0 from in0, bit 1 from in1, and bit 2 from in2.

BLOCK_WORD_COUNTER counts words within a data block, asserts start/end-of-block markers, and emits a two-word block header. Its inputs are clock, reset, restart, and word-ready; outputs are end-of-block flag, 16-bit header word, header-ready, and block-count-ready. A 10-bit counter increments on each ready word, resets at block boundaries, and triggers EOB at the block word limit. A 5-bit sequence number advances on EOB/restart, and the header packs a fixed pattern with sequence, GBTid, egroupID, and epathID. Start-of-block produces two ready pulses that output the upper then lower header halves.

This module converts 10-bit input data into a stream of 4-bit output nibbles, driving a request/trigger handshake to fetch each new value. Its ports include bitCLK, bitCLKx4, and reset inputs, edataIN and edataINrdy data inputs, and getDataTrig and EddataOUT outputs. A toggle counter on bitCLK creates a two-cycle request, which is pulse-shaped by bitCLKx4 to form getDataTrig. A delayed version of that request latches edataIN’s lower byte and resets a select counter, and a 2:1 mux alternately outputs the low and high nibbles.

This module is a clock divider that generates a slow, nominally 2 Hz output clock. Its inputs are CLK_IN and an active-high asynchronous RST, and its output is CLK_OUT. A 32-bit counter increments on each rising edge of CLK_IN. When the count reaches 25,000,000, an internal register toggles and the counter resets, so CLK_OUT changes state every that many input cycles. Asserting RST asynchronously clears both the counter and the output register to zero.

This module wraps a character-memory block with an on-chip stimulus generator and status monitor. Its ports are CLK_IN (clock), RESET_IN (reset), and a 9-bit registered STATUS output. Reset is synchronized through three flip-flops; a BMG_STIM_GEN instance drives the char_mem_exdes memory, whose read address is a delayed copy of the address bus. An issue flag is OR-accumulated into STATUS[7:0] until reset, while a counter bit, shifted through a pipeline, drives STATUS[8].

C2 is a purely combinational module that computes the bitwise OR of two 8-bit values. It has two 8-bit input ports, A and B, and one 8-bit output port, F. Internally, a single continuous assignment drives F with A OR B, so each output bit is the logical OR of the corresponding input bits. There are no clocks, resets, or sequential elements.

MUX_wm is a 6-bit 2:1 multiplexer that selects between two 6-bit inputs based on a control signal. Its inputs are RDin, o15, and the one-bit select RFDest, while its output is the 6-bit nRD. When RFDest is high, nRD is driven by o15; otherwise nRD follows RDin. The selection is combinational and updates whenever any input changes.
Response:
module MUX_wm(
input wire [5:0] RDin,
input wire [5:0] o15,
input wire RFDest,
output reg [5:0] nRD
);
  always @(RDin, RFDest, o15) begin
    if((RFDest == 1'b1)) begin
      nRD <= o15;
    end
    else begin
      nRD <= RDin;
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module computes a 27-bit result from two 27-bit unsigned inputs, effectively calculating (in_a + in_b + 1) with the least significant bit discarded, i.e. a rounded right shift by one. Its ports are the 27-bit result output and the 27-bit inputs in_a and in_b. Internally, both inputs are zero-extended to 29 bits, with a constant 1 appended to in_a and 0 appended to in_b. The two 29-bit values are added, and bits 27 through 1 of the sum become the output, dropping the LSB and the overflow bit.

This module is a top-level controller for an 8x8 LED display, arranged as two 8-bit output vectors, that shows a heart pattern and an auxiliary logic-driven LED under button and PWM control.

Its inputs are clocks `clk` and `clk_dv`, reset, a PWM enable, and five pushbuttons; its outputs are the 8-bit LED column/row vectors `led_x` and `led_y`.

Internally, it debounces the five buttons, then uses the debounced signals to configure a PWM generator and an 8x8 heart-pattern generator.

When PWM is disabled, each LED output combines the PWM logic signal with the heart pattern via OR; when PWM is enabled, only the heart pattern drives the LEDs.

clock_generator produces a gated, divided version of clock, with divide ratio set by parameter GV_CLOCK_DIV (default 50). Its ports are clock, reset_n, enable, and clock_out. A counter increments on each clock while enable is high, resetting when enable is low or after reaching GV_CLOCK_DIV-1. clock_out is high only when enable is high and the counter is at least half the divide value, giving a roughly 50% duty-cycle gated clock. Note: reset_n is intended as an active-low asynchronous reset, but the edge/level condition used is not a standard implementation.

fp_log is a clocked pipelined natural-logarithm unit for a floating-point operand, outputting sign, 8-bit exponent, 23-bit mantissa, and NaN/overflow/zero flags. Its inputs are sysclk, reset, enable, and the sign/exponent/mantissa operand. When enabled it registers the operand, uses OR/AND reduction chains to detect zero mantissa, zero exponent, and max-exponent cases, and shifts NaN/infinity indicators through a delay chain matching the pipeline depth. An fp_ln_core computes the log, and fp_lnrnd rounds the result and generates the final status outputs.

logic1 is a combinational logic module that sets its output based on priority input conditions. Its ports are single-bit inputs A, B, and C, plus a single-bit output F. If A is high, F is driven high regardless of B and C. Otherwise, if both B and C are high, F is driven low. For all other input combinations, F is assigned an unknown value to prevent unintended latch inference.

This module implements an 8-to-1 tristate multiplexer using active-low select signals. Its inputs are an 8-bit data bus `di` and an 8-bit select bus `sel`, with a single-bit output `do`. Each select bit enables one corresponding data bit onto the shared output; when a select bit is high, that driver is placed in high-impedance state. The design assumes only one select bit is asserted low at a time, so `do` follows that selected data bit, otherwise it floats.

This module drives a multiplexed four-digit seven-segment display from four 4-bit hexadecimal inputs. Inputs are RESET, GCLKP1, and LED0–LED3; outputs are LEDOut (segment pattern) and DigitSelect (digit enable). A clock divider generates a strobe, and a 2-bit counter cycles through the four digits. The selected nibble is decoded into a seven-segment pattern, while DigitSelect activates the matching display digit. RESET clears the counter and digit-select state.

The module `issue` is intended as a simple combinational buffer. It has one input, `i_foo`, and one output, `o_foo`. Internally it defines a parameter, `k_foo`, set from the input, then drives the output with that parameter XORed with zero, effectively passing it through. However, initializing a parameter from a runtime input is not legal Verilog, so the module is invalid and non-synthesizable.

This module is a UART receiver controller that deserializes an asynchronous serial input into an 8-bit byte. Its inputs are UART_RX, CLK, and RESET_READ; its outputs are DATA[7:0] and READ_DATA. A baud-rate counter derived from FREQ and BAUD detects a low start bit, samples the eight data bits at their centers into a shift register, and checks the stop bit. When a valid high stop bit is seen, the received byte is latched to DATA and READ_DATA is asserted; RESET_READ clears READ_DATA.

This is a streaming non-maximum-suppression stage for a VGA pixel pipeline. It passes a 32-bit Hessian response unless any of eight surrounding responses is larger, in which case it outputs zero. Inputs are clk, enable, active, x/y pixel addresses, and hessian_in; outputs are registered delayed x/y addresses and hessian_out. Internally, a shift register stores recent values; while active, the center value is compared with its neighbors. Comparisons occur only when enable is high, and output addresses lag inputs by one pixel.

This module converts an 8-bit switch input into two seven-segment display outputs. Its ports are an 8-bit switch input plus rightSeg and leftSeg 8-bit outputs. Internally, the input is split into two 4-bit nibbles; each nibble is bit-reversed and inverted before being passed to a binToSeg converter instance. The lower four switches drive the left display, while the upper four drive the right display.

This module is a GMII receive-path test block that captures incoming Ethernet RX bytes and reports the number of received packets on LEDs. Its ports include button inputs, LED outputs, a GMII PHY interface for management, transmit, and receive, plus a differential system clock input. Internally, valid RX data bytes are stored into a block RAM using a byte-write counter, while the RX data-valid signal is edge-detected to increment a packet counter and latch a packet-read flag. The GMII transmit and management outputs are held idle, and the GMII TX clock is generated from the system clock using a clocking primitive and DDR output. The RX error, carrier-sense, and collision inputs, as well as the buttons, are otherwise unused.

TOP_EQ is a top-level bridge that displays 16-bit bus data on a multiplexed seven-segment display and interfaces an external memory-style bus. Inputs are CLK, NWE, NE, NOE, and a bidirectional 16-bit DATA bus; outputs are 4-bit ANODES, 8-bit CATHODES, RDY, plus buffered NWE_OUT, NE_OUT, NOE_OUT, and RDY_OUT. A clock wizard derives synchronized clocks and a LOCKED reset from CLK. A frequency divider generates a display-enable pulse for the seven-segment driver, while an FSMC block handles bus control and produces RDY. Control outputs directly mirror the corresponding inputs.

This module performs a 32-bit subtraction, producing `result = in_a − in_b` modulo 2^32. It has two 32-bit inputs, `in_a` and `in_b`, and one 32-bit output, `result`. Internally, each input is zero-extended and shifted left by one bit to form 34-bit operands, which are then subtracted. The 32-bit slice from bit 1 through bit 32 of the 34-bit difference is returned as `result`, discarding the inserted low bit. No carry, borrow, or overflow output is provided.

This module implements a combinational unsigned 32×32 multiplier that produces a 64-bit product. It takes two 32-bit inputs, a and b, and drives a 64-bit registered output op whenever either input changes. Internally it uses a shift-and-add algorithm: a running sum accumulates the multiplicand when the multiplier's least-significant bit is set, then the multiplicand shifts left and the multiplier shifts right each iteration. The loop runs 33 times, and the accumulation uses the original a and b rather than the shifted copies, with no explicit initialization of the result register, so the computed product may be incorrect.

This module implements a 4-to-1 multiplexer that routes one of four data inputs to a single output based on a 2-bit select signal. Its inputs are a, b, c, and d (data) plus sel (2-bit selector), and its output is y. Internally, a continuous assignment uses nested conditional selection: sel=00 selects a, 01 selects b, 10 selects c, and 11 selects d.

The module implements a purely combinational two-input exclusive-OR function: output f is high when x1 and x2 differ, and low when they match. Its ports are 1-bit inputs x1 and x2 and a 1-bit output f. Internally, f is formed from two AND terms—one using x1 with the inverse of x2 and the other using the inverse of x1 with x2—combined by OR. A local wire named tmp is tied low but unused. There are no clocks, resets, or state elements.

An 8-bit up-counter that raises its done flag once the count reaches 138 (0x8A). Inputs are clk, rst, set_zero, and start; the single output fin reports completion. A separate 8-bit incrementer supplies the next count value. The sequential block asynchronously clears the counter and flag on rst or set_zero, latches fin high and holds the count when 138 is reached, increments on start, and otherwise holds its state.

SOMA is an 8-bit ripple-carry adder. It takes two 8-bit inputs, A and B, and produces an 8-bit sum output F plus a 4-bit Flag output. Internally, eight full-adder stages are chained by carry signals, with B passed unchanged into each stage. The flags report zero, signed overflow, carry-out, and negative/sign conditions.

This module generates read and write enable control signals for a register file based on two 4-bit opcode inputs. Its ports are CLK (unused), OPC and OPC4 inputs, plus registered outputs RD_EN and WR_EN. Both outputs are driven combinationally by separate case statements on OPC and OPC4. RD_EN is asserted high for every OPC value, so reads are always enabled. WR_EN is asserted for most OPC4 codes but deasserted for the default and certain excluded opcodes.

This module is intended as a 2-to-4 binary decoder, asserting one of four outputs based on a two-bit input. It has two 1-bit inputs, i0 and i1, and four 1-bit outputs, o0 through o3. Internally, four AND terms combine the true or complemented inputs to form a one-hot decode. However, the assignments drive signals named out0–out3 rather than the declared outputs o0–o3, so the actual outputs are left undriven.

This module is a combinational 16-bit ALU that drives a result bus. Its inputs are clock, reset, an operation select, an output-enable (to_bus_e), and 16-bit operands A and B; its only output is the 16-bit result. When to_bus_e is high, result is A plus B if operation is 0, otherwise A minus B. When to_bus_e is low, result is forced to zero. Clock, reset, and the internal z wire are unused, so the block reacts only to its listed combinational inputs.
Response:
module TestCPU1_ALU(
input wire clock,
input wire reset,
input wire operation,
input wire to_bus_e,
input wire [15:0] A,
input wire [15:0] B,
output reg [15:0] result
);
wire z;
  always @(to_bus_e, operation, A, B) begin
    if(to_bus_e == 1'b1) begin
      if(operation == 1'b0) begin
        result <= A + B;
      end
      else begin
        result <= A - B;
      end
    end
    else begin
      result <= 16'h0000;
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module is an RS-232/UART transmitter that serially sends an 8-bit byte at 115200 baud. Its inputs are a 115200 Hz clock, a send-start pulse, and the 8-bit data to transmit; its outputs are an acknowledge signal and the serial output line. An internal four-state finite state machine handles idle, start bit, data transmission, and stop bit. On start, it drives a low start bit, shifts out the data LSB-first, then drives a high stop bit and asserts acknowledge before returning to idle.

This module implements a 1-bit full adder. It takes two data inputs and a carry-in, producing a sum bit and a carry-out bit. Internally, it XORs the two data inputs for the sum path and ANDs them to generate a carry. The carry-out combines this generated carry with the propagate term formed from the input XOR and carry-in.

This module drives a seven-segment display, cycling through hexadecimal digits 0–F. It takes a clock input and produces an 8-bit `segment_data` output. Internally, a 16-bit counter increments on each clock; when it wraps to zero, a 4-bit `number` register increments. The output is a combinational lookup that maps the current `number` to its corresponding active-low segment pattern.

This module is a 16-bit 3-to-1 multiplexer that drives `DATAOUT` from one of three 16-bit sources based on two select inputs. Its inputs are `SHOWA1A0`, `SHOWA3A2`, `OUTPUT`, `SHOW1OUT`, and `SHOW2OUT`; `DATAOUT` is the 16-bit output. Internally, a combinational block gives `SHOWA1A0` highest priority: when asserted, `DATAOUT` follows `SHOW1OUT`. Otherwise, if `SHOWA3A2` is asserted, `DATAOUT` follows `SHOW2OUT`; if neither select is asserted, `DATAOUT` follows `OUTPUT`.
Response:
module MUX(
input wire SHOWA1A0,
input wire SHOWA3A2,
input wire [15:0] OUTPUT,
input wire [15:0] SHOW1OUT,
input wire [15:0] SHOW2OUT,
output reg [15:0] DATAOUT
);
  always @(SHOWA1A0, SHOWA3A2, SHOW1OUT, SHOW2OUT, OUTPUT) begin
    if(SHOWA1A0 == 1'b1) begin
      DATAOUT <= SHOW1OUT;
    end
    else if(SHOWA3A2 == 1'b1) begin
      DATAOUT <= SHOW2OUT;
    end
    else begin
      DATAOUT <= OUTPUT;
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module implements a 32-bit combinational adder. It has two 32-bit input ports, value1 and value2, and one 32-bit output port, result. Whenever either input changes, the internal logic recalculates result as their sum. Because it uses only combinational sensitivity and no clock, the output reflects the addition continuously after input updates.

This module is a pipeline register that carries memory-stage signals into the writeback stage. Its inputs are clk, reset, and four pipeline signals: RegWE_in, RegDest_in (4-bit), RegWriteVal_in (16-bit), and MemRd_in; the corresponding outputs are registered versions of these. On the asynchronous active-low reset (triggered by a rising edge on reset), the outputs are cleared: write-enable and memory-read flags go low, the destination becomes all ones, and the write value becomes zero. Otherwise, on each rising clock edge, all inputs are captured into the outputs.

This module is a purely combinational 20-bit adder that computes the lower 20 bits of the sum of its two inputs, effectively ignoring any carry beyond bit 19. It has two 20-bit inputs, `in_a` and `in_b`, and a 20-bit output, `result`. Internally, it appends a constant LSB of 1 to `in_a` and 0 to `in_b`, forming two 22-bit values. These values are added, and bits [20:1] of the sum are selected as `result`, which yields `(in_a + in_b) mod 2^20`.

This module is a simple 8-bit passthrough that connects its switch inputs directly to its LED outputs. It has an 8-bit input bus for the switches and an 8-bit output bus for the LEDs. Internally, it uses purely combinational logic with no clock, reset, or state; each output bit continuously reflects the corresponding input bit.

Packed halfword SIMD adder: it treats two 64-bit operands as four independent unsigned 16-bit lanes and produces a 64-bit result. Ports: rs1 and rs2 are the 64-bit inputs; rd is the 64-bit output. Each lane sum is computed in a 17-bit temporary to retain the carry, and is clamped to 65535 when it exceeds 65536, so a sum of exactly 65536 is not clamped and wraps. The four clamped low halfwords are then concatenated into rd.

This is a top-level wrapper for an AC97 audio interface core. Inputs are ClkIn and active-low Reset_n; outputs are LED[3:0], DEBUG[4:0], AC97Reset_n, Sync, and SData_Out, with AC97Clk and SData_In as codec clock/input. Internally, zero-valued playback samples are pipelined through two registers before feeding an ac97_if submodule, which generates the codec control/data signals and debug outputs. LEDs invert the core's debug bits, and DEBUG exposes AC97Clk, reset, sync, and serial-data lines.

Clocked finite-state machine that converts serial Gray-coded bits into a 3-bit angle increment. Its inputs are clk, reset, a 1-bit data input, a data-valid qualifier, and a 3-bit modulation selector; outputs are the 3-bit increment and a valid pulse. It collects the required number of bits depending on modulation, moving through three bit-collection states before asserting the output-valid state. Each accepted bit is Gray-to-binary decoded using XOR with accumulated bits, then registered on the clock; reset clears the accumulator and returns to the idle state.

This module debounces four independent button inputs and outputs a corresponding four-bit pulse signal. Its inputs are a clock and a 4-bit button bus, and its output is a 4-bit pulse bus. Internally, four debounce instances each process one button using the clock, producing intermediate debounced signals. Those signals are then conditionally assigned to the output bus, effectively passing each debounced button state through as a pulse.

This module implements a single-bit buffer. It has one input, a, and one output, b, both one-bit wires. Internally, the output is continuously driven to match the input, so b always equals a. It contains no state, clock, or additional logic. Functionally, it simply propagates its input signal to its output.

This module is a 4-bit two-to-one multiplexer. It has a one-bit select input `ctrl`, two 4-bit data inputs `a` and `b`, a 4-bit output `s`, and supply pins `vdd` and `vss`. The output follows `a` when `ctrl` is low and follows `b` when `ctrl` is high. The supply pins are not used by the implemented selection logic.

This module implements a two-input NOR gate. It has two 1-bit input ports, a and b, and one 1-bit output port, q. The output is driven combinationally so that q is high only when both inputs are low; if either input is high, q is low. Internally, it ORs the inputs and inverts the result.

This module implements a single positive-edge-triggered D flip-flop. It has a clock input, an active-low reset input, a data input, and a registered data output. On each rising clock edge, the stored output value updates to the current data input. The reset signal is present but unused, so it does not affect operation. The output continuously reflects the internal stored state, which initializes to logic zero.

This module bridges parallel audio samples and an I2S serial bus, converting between them in both directions. Inputs: clk, 16-bit left/right audio in, i2s_bclk, i2s_d_in, i2s_lr; outputs: 16-bit left/right audio out, new_sample, i2s_d_out. Internally it delays i2s_bclk to detect valid-data and output-change edges; a 127-bit register captures serial input, and a 64-bit register serializes output. On an LR rising edge it latches received left/right words to the outputs, reloads the output register with the input samples padded by zeros, and pulses new_sample.

This module implements a 4-to-1 multiplexer that selects one of four 4-bit data inputs. It has four 4-bit inputs w, x, y, and z, a 2-bit select input s, and a 4-bit output m. The selection is purely combinational: when s is 00, m is w; 01 selects x; 10 selects y; and 11 selects z. Thus m continuously reflects the chosen input word.

Implements a configurable internal ROM and RAM subsystem, with ROM and RAM sizes selected by parameters. Ports include clock/reset_n, ROM address/request and data/complete, and RAM address/write enable/data in/data/request/complete. Request signals are registered on clock to generate completion outputs. ROM logic uses generate blocks: parameter 3 decodes two small OS ROMs, 2 uses a looping 16K ROM, 1 selects between a 16K OS and BASIC ROM, and 0 returns no ROM. RAM is either a generic inferred RAM (when size >0) or tied off; reset is asynchronous active-low.

This module is a purely combinational color-depth converter that maps a 16-bit RGB565 pixel value to a 12-bit VGA output. It takes a single 16-bit input `rgb565` and produces three 4-bit outputs `vga_r`, `vga_g`, and `vga_b`. Internally, the input is split into 5-bit red, 6-bit green, and 5-bit blue fields, and each field is truncated to its upper (most significant) four bits to form the corresponding VGA channel. No clock or state is involved.

This module is a combinational 4-bit to 7-segment display decoder. Its input U_NUMBER is a 4-bit digit value, and its output SEGMENTS is a 7-bit active-low segment control bus. Each segment is assigned directly from equality and greater-than comparisons on U_NUMBER, lighting the correct segments for decimal digits 0–9 and producing extended patterns for values above 9. There is no clock, reset, or internal state.

This module combines two single-bit inputs into one two-bit output, using the first input as the upper bit and the second as the lower bit. It has inputs a and b, both 1-bit, and a 2-bit output z. Internally, a continuous assignment drives z with the ordered pair a followed by b.

An 8-bit ALU (ULA) whose operation is chosen by a 3-bit opcode. It accepts two 8-bit operands, X and Y, along with sel_ula, and outputs an 8-bit result plus zero (Z) and negative (N) flags. Internally the operands are zero-extended to 9 bits so the adder's carry is preserved, and a multiplexer selects among addition, AND, OR, bitwise NOT of X, pass-through of Y, a right shift, a left shift, or addition again. Z is asserted when the low eight result bits are all zero, while N reflects result bit 7.

This module implements an 8-word by 8-bit RAM. Its inputs are chip select `cs`, read/write `rw`, 3-bit address `dir`, and 8-bit `data_in`; `data_out` is the 8-bit output. When `cs` is high, `rw` low reads the addressed memory word onto `data_out`, while `rw` high writes `data_in` into that word. When `cs` is low, `data_out` is placed in high impedance. The logic is sensitive to changes on `cs`, `rw`, `dir`, or `data_in`.

This module is a UART receiver that samples a serial input and outputs one 8-bit byte with a data-available flag. Its inputs are clock, reset, serial receive line, receive clock enable, and read strobe; outputs are the received byte and data-available signal. Internally, a majority filter cleans the receive line, and a baud-rate generator produces sampling ticks. A four-state machine waits for a start bit, shifts in eight data bits, then validates the stop bit and asserts data-available until read clears it.

Cntrl_cont is a 3-bit synchronous up-counter with a synchronous reset. It has a clock input clk, an active-high reset input reset, and a 3-bit output sal_cont. Internally, a 3-bit register increments by one on each rising clock edge. When reset is high at a clock edge, the register clears to zero. The output continuously reflects the register value.

This 16-bit arithmetic unit adds or subtracts two operands, producing a result and status flags. Inputs are operands RA and RB plus a 3-bit opcode OP; outputs are 16-bit AR_OUT and 4-bit SREG_OUT. Operands are zero-extended to 17 bits, and a combinational case selects addition for opcodes 000/101, subtraction for 001, else zero. Flags derive from the 17-bit result: negative, zero, signed overflow, and carry.

Reset controller for an AXI/GTX/PHY design. Inputs are s_axi_aclk, gtx_clk, glbl_rst, rx_reset, tx_reset, and dcm_locked; outputs are glbl_rst_intn, gtx_resetn, s_axi_resetn, and phy_resetn. It synchronizes dcm_locked, uses reset synchronizers to create clock-domain resets, and combines rx_reset, tx_reset, and glbl_rst for the GTX domain. Two-stage flip-flops produce fully synchronous active-low AXI and GTX resets, while a 6-bit counter delays PHY reset release.

This module is a clock-and-reset wrapper for a VP780 device that instantiates the `clkrst_vp780` primitive to generate the system clocks and resets.

Its inputs are differential 200 MHz and 300 MHz reference pairs, an auxiliary clock, two synthesized clocks, an external reset, and a 64-bit command interface with a command clock and valid signal; its outputs are a 64-bit command response with valid, a 32-bit clock-output vector, and a 32-bit reset-output vector.

The primitive generates 200 MHz and 300 MHz clocks along with multiple phase-shifted synthesized clocks (0/90/180/270 and divided variants), DDR clocks, DDR capture clocks, and three reset outputs, while forwarding the command interface through unchanged.

The wrapper maps those generated clocks and resets onto selected bits of the 32-bit output vectors, replicates the 200 MHz clock on two outputs and the 300 MHz clock on one, drives the DDR capture reset to one reset bit, leaves the primitive's delay-ready output unconnected, and ties the unused upper reset bits low.

This module generates 640x480 VGA timing: it produces horizontal and vertical sync pulses, a video-enable, and pixel/line counters from a pixel clock.

Ports: inputs clk and asynchronous clear clr; outputs hsync, vsync, 10-bit hc and vc counters, 23-bit pix counter, and vidon.

Internally, a horizontal counter cycles 0–799 and clocks a vertical counter through 521 lines; sync outputs go low during each blanking region.

vidon is asserted only inside the active video window between the horizontal and vertical back/front porches, and pix counts active pixels, clearing at frame end.

This module is the ALU control decoder for a MIPS-like processor, translating opcode and function fields into a 3-bit ALU operation. It has two inputs, the 2-bit ULAOp and the 6-bit funct, and one 3-bit output, Operacao. When ULAOp is 00 or 01, the output is fixed to 010 or 110, forcing add or subtract. Otherwise, the output is chosen from funct bits in priority order: bit 3 selects 111, bit 0 selects 001, bit 2 selects 000, and bit 1 selects 010 when low, else 110.

Converts a 4-bit binary value into a 7-segment display pattern. It has a 4-bit input `bin` and a 7-bit registered output `seg`, one bit per segment. A purely combinational case statement maps decimal digits 0–9 to active-low segment codes, while all other input values produce a blank display via the default case.

Module B2A converts a 4-bit binary value into an 8-bit code. It has a 4-bit input D and an 8-bit output A. Internally, the upper four bits of A are fixed to 0011 (hex 3), while the lower four bits are directly driven by D. Thus A equals 0x30 plus D, producing ASCII digits 0–9 for D=0–9 and other 0x3x codes for D=10–15.

ImageFilter is a streaming 3x3 convolution engine: it delays the 8-bit pixel input through FlipFlop stages and two FIFO line buffers to assemble a 3x3 neighborhood, then the kernel module weights those nine pixels by coefficients m1–m9 and produces the scaled output. Its ports are 8-bit Din, CLK, RESET, WR_EN, nine 4-bit coefficients, divider_selector, plus outputs RD_EN and 8-bit Dout. A control counter increments while WR_EN is high, asserts RD_EN only after 138 write cycles, and clears RD_EN when WR_EN goes low.

Instruction: This module is a clock-generation wrapper that uses a DCM primitive to synthesize an output clock from CLKIN_IN. It has one input, CLKIN_IN, and three outputs: CLK0_OUT, CLK0_OUT1, and CLK2X_OUT. The DCM is configured for frequency synthesis with an 11/14 multiply/divide ratio, no feedback or phase shifting, and low-frequency modes; its control and status inputs are tied inactive. Only the CLKFX output is used, routed through a global buffer to drive CLK0_OUT. CLK0_OUT1 and CLK2X_OUT are left undriven.

output wire CLK0_OUT,
output wire CLK0_OUT1,
output wire CLK2X_OUT

      .I(CLKFX_BUF),
    .O(CLK0_OUT));
  DCM #(
      .CLK_FEEDBACK(4'bNONE),
    .CLKDV_DIVIDE(4.0),
    // 25.175 = 32 * 11 / 14
    .CLKFX_DIVIDE(14),
    .CLKFX_MULTIPLY(11),

Instruction: The module is a clock manager that derives two slower clocks from a 50 MHz input. Its inputs are clk50 and an asynchronous reset rst, and its outputs are clk12 and clk25. An 8-bit counter increments on each rising clk50 edge and is cleared when rst is high. The counter’s lowest bit drives clk25, and its next bit drives clk12, producing divide-by-2 and divide-by-4 clocks.

This module converts a 4-bit binary value into its equivalent 4-bit Gray code. It has a 4-bit binary input and a 4-bit Gray-code output. The most significant output bit directly follows the most significant input bit. Each lower output bit is generated by XORing adjacent input bits. The output updates whenever the binary input changes.

This module implements a single-bit D flip-flop with asynchronous active-low reset, often used as a basic synchronizer stage. Its inputs are NRST, CLK, and D, and its registered output is Q. The internal always block triggers on either a falling CLK edge or a falling NRST edge. When NRST is low, Q is cleared to zero; otherwise, on each falling CLK edge, Q captures the value of D.

This module is a combinational 32-bit adder that produces the sum of its two inputs, discarding any carry out. It has three ports: 32-bit inputs `in_a` and `in_b`, and a 32-bit output `result`. Internally both operands are widened to 34 bits by appending a low bit — a '1' to `in_a` and a '0' to `in_b` — so the sum effectively injects a carry-in of one. The widened sum is computed, and its middle 32 bits (positions 32 down to 1) form the output, yielding `in_a + in_b` modulo 2^32.

The module implements a single-bit combinational AND gate. It has two 1-bit input ports, `a` and `b`, and one 1-bit output port, `c`. Internally, the output is continuously driven by the logical AND of the two inputs, so `c` is high only when both `a` and `b` are high; otherwise it is low.

This module is the main control unit of a MIPS-style processor datapath, decoding a 6-bit opcode into datapath control signals. Its inputs are Op5 through Op0, and its outputs are RegDst, ALUSrc, MemtoReg, RegWrite, MemRead, MemWrite, Branch, ALUOp1, and ALUOp0. Internally it combinationally recognizes four instruction types — R-format, lw, sw, and beq — by ANDing selected opcode bits (with inversion), then derives each output from those decoded flags. For example, MemRead and MemtoReg are asserted only for lw, MemWrite only for sw, and Branch only for beq.

The module is combinational and effectively acts as an 8-bit pass-through: `out_word` equals `in_word`. It has one 8-bit input, `in_word`, and one 8-bit output, `out_word`, updated whenever the input changes. Internally, it copies the input into an 8-bit temporary and zero-extends that into a 32-bit integer. It then concatenates the top two input bits with the integer and the temporary, but because the concatenation is wider than the output, only the low eight bits are retained—which are the original input.

This module is an EX/MEM pipeline segment register that latches execution-stage data and control signals while its write-enable input is high; because it is level-sensitive, outputs follow inputs when enabled and hold when disabled. It has a clock, a write-enable, and 16-bit/2-bit inputs for ALU result, register Ry, immediate, source-result select, memory write enable, register write enable, and write-result select, with matching registered outputs. Most outputs are conditionally assigned from the inputs; the `we_result_out` port is an undriven wire. There is no reset or clock-edge behavior.

      ex_mem_segment_regfile_mem_we_out <= ex_mem_segment_regfile_mem_we_in;
      ex_mem_segment_regfile_src_result_out <= ex_mem_segment_regfile_src_result_in;
      ex_mem_segment_regfile_reg_we_out <= ex_mem_segment_regfile_reg_we_in;
      ex_mem_segment_regfile_imm_out <= ex_mem_segment_regfile_imm_in;
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module is a clocked button debouncer that filters a raw mechanical input and produces a clean output pulse. It has a clock input `CLK`, a raw button input `BUTTON`, and an output `DOUT`. Internally, a 24-bit saturating up/down counter increments while `BUTTON` is high and decrements while it is low, synchronized to `CLK`. A small shift register tracks whether the counter is zero or nonzero, and `DOUT` is asserted for one clock cycle when that history indicates the counter has just returned to zero after being nonzero—flagging a debounced transition back to the low/zero state.

watchdog_timer monitors an OPB bus transaction and raises OPB_timeout if a selected transfer does not complete in time. Its inputs are OPB_select, OPB_xferAck, OPB_retry, OPB_toutSup, Clk, and Rst; OPB_timeout is the registered output. A 4-bit counter increments each clock while OPB_select is asserted and both OPB_xferAck and OPB_retry are low; OPB_toutSup pauses counting, while reset or any other condition clears it. When the count reaches OPB_TIMEOUT_CNT-2 under those same conditions, OPB_timeout is asserted for one clock.

This module computes the next program counter value by incrementing the current program counter. It has a 16-bit input PC and a 16-bit registered output NPC. Internally, NPC is updated whenever PC changes, assigning PC plus one. It is purely combinational and has no clock or reset.

This module implements a single-bit logical inverter. It has one 1-bit input port named input and one 1-bit output port named output. Its internal logic is purely combinational. When the input is low, the output is driven high; otherwise the output is driven low. Thus, the output is the Boolean complement of the input.

This parameterized VGA timing generator produces 640x480 video timing from a 25 MHz pixel clock. It takes clk_25 and rst as inputs, and outputs active, hsync, vsync, plus 10-bit pixel coordinates xaddr and yaddr. Two counters track horizontal and vertical positions using parameterized visible-size, front-porch, back-porch, and retrace delays. The sync outputs are registered to avoid glitches, and active is asserted only within the visible 640x480 region.

This module is a combinational unsigned multiplier that computes the product of two input operands and outputs the low 32 bits. Its ports are a 32-bit input, a 15-bit input, and a 32-bit output. Internally, it forms a 47-bit product from the two inputs, then selects the lower 32 bits of that product as the final result.

C1 is a combinational 4-bit binary adder. It has two 4-bit inputs, A and B, and one 4-bit output, F. Internally, F continuously reflects the sum of A and B. Because F is also 4 bits wide, any carry beyond the fourth bit is discarded.

This module is a two-phase coprocessor: on the first valid input it stores byte 1 as a reference minimum and echoes the word; later valid inputs are meant to be scaled against that minimum. Ports are clock, async reset, 32-bit INPUT_1 with a valid strobe, and registered 32-bit OUTPUT_1. A store_min_beta flag switches between the capture and transform phases. The transform datapath is effectively inoperative: beta_tmp is tied to zero and OUTPUT_1_tmp is never driven, so later outputs are undefined.

This module implements a 16-bit parallel register of D flip-flops. It has inputs clock, reset, enable, and a 16-bit data input, plus a 16-bit registered output. The internal always block is triggered by positive edges of clock, reset, enable, or input changes, so reset is asynchronous. Reset has priority: when high, the output is cleared to all zeros. Otherwise, when enable is high, the input is captured; when enable is low, the output holds its value.
Response:
module RegisterDFlipFlop_x16(
input wire clock,
input wire reset,
input wire enable,
input wire [15:0] input,
output reg [15:0] output
);
  always @(posedge clock, posedge reset, posedge enable, posedge input) begin
    if((reset == 1'b1)) begin
      output <= 16'b0000000000000000;
    end else begin
      if((enable == 1'b1)) begin
        output <= input;
      end
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module wraps a RAT_MCU processor, mapping its simple I/O port interface to board switches, buttons, LEDs, seven-segment displays, and display enables. It outputs 8-bit LED and segment values plus a 4-bit display enable, and inputs 8-bit switches, 4-bit buttons, reset, and clock. Internally, the MCU’s port ID selects either the switches or lower button bits as its input, while its output-port strobe and ID latch MCU writes into separate LED, segment, and display-enable registers that drive the outputs.

This module implements a clocked 2:1 multiplexer whose select input is gated by its own output and registered. Inputs are clock, active-low reset, data inputs A and B, and select Sel; the single output is O. The select term is formed as Sel AND the current output, then captured in a D flip-flop on the clock edge, with reset clearing it. The registered select drives the multiplexer, which passes either A or B to O.

This module converts a single 4-bit BCD digit into an 8-bit binary output. It has a 4-bit input `bcd` and an 8-bit output `binary`. Internally, the lower four output bits are directly driven by the input, while the upper four bits are tied to zero. It therefore performs a zero-extension rather than multi-digit BCD-to-binary conversion.

Generates an 18-bit SRAM write address that increments on each horizontal reference pulse and resets at frame boundaries. Inputs are pclk, href, vsync, and module_enable; outputs are ack and the 18-bit sram_addr. Internally, a registered address buffer drives sram_addr and is triggered asynchronously by rising edges of any input. When module_enable is low the address clears; otherwise href high increments it. A vsync high resets the address and asserts ack, taking priority over other actions.

This module is a routing interconnect that steers data between two SPI ports and two FIFOs, acting as a steering hub for each channel. Each channel has a master-side interface (16-bit data in/out, write-enable, read-request input, and data-ready output) and an SPI-side interface (16-bit data out/in, write-enable out, data-ready in). On the SPI-to-master path, a read request captures SPI input directly onto the master data output, while the absence of a request forwards SPI data into the corresponding FIFO with the SPI ready signal as the write enable. On the master-to-SPI path, control and write signals pass through unchanged, and data-ready outputs are driven directly by the SPI ready inputs.

This module implements a combinational two-input AND gate. It has two 1-bit input ports, a and b, and one 1-bit output port, c. Internally, c is continuously driven by the logical AND of the two inputs, so it is high only when both a and b are high. The design contains no state, clock, or sequential logic.

This module generates a periodic single-cycle tick pulse from a clock. It has inputs clk and asynchronous active-high reset, plus a tick output. A 32-bit counter increments each clock and wraps to zero after reaching the parameter M minus one. The tick output is asserted combinationally only during the cycle when the counter is at its terminal value.

This module implements a combinational 16-bit binary adder, producing the low 16 bits of X + Y. Its inputs are two 16-bit operands, X and Y, and its output is the 16-bit sum Z. Internally, a 5-bit carry vector starts with carry-in zero, and a generate loop instantiates four 4-bit adders. Each adder processes a 4-bit slice of X and Y and passes its carry to the next stage, creating a ripple-carry chain; the final carry-out is unused.

This module is a synchronous loadable up-counter for a memory address. Its inputs are clock, a 24-bit load_value, load enable do_load, and increment enable do_inc; its output is the current address. On each rising clock edge, do_load loads load_value into an internal register, otherwise do_inc increments it by one, otherwise it holds. Load has priority over increment, and the register drives the address output continuously.

This module is a single-bit delay generator that reproduces an incoming pulse after a programmable number of clock cycles. Its ports are clock `clk`, synchronous/asynchronous reset `rst`, input `bit_in`, and registered output `bit_out`; the parameter `CYCLES` (default 15) sets the delay length. A three-state FSM waits in IDLE for a high input, counts clock cycles in DELAY_CNT until the count reaches `CYCLES`, then asserts `bit_out` high for one cycle in DELAY_ASSERT before returning to IDLE. Reset initializes the state, counter, and output to zero, and the output defaults low each cycle unless asserted.

This module generates divided VGA clock signals from a single 200 MHz input. Its input is `clk_200`, and its outputs are `clk_100`, `clk_50`, `clk_25`, and `clk_12_5`, corresponding to 100, 50, 25, and 12.5 MHz. Internally, it uses a cascade of toggle flip-flops, where each stage toggles on the rising edge of the previous stage’s clock. This successively halves the frequency at each stage, producing the four output clocks.

This debouncer filters a mechanical switch input into a clean, registered output. Its inputs are clk, reset, and switch, and its only output is the debounced level. A 19-bit counter free-runs to generate a periodic tick every 2^19 clock cycles, providing the timing base. An eight-state FSM waits multiple tick intervals after reset or an output change, then samples switch and updates output only when the sampled level matches the new target. Clocked state/counter registers and combinational next-state logic implement this delayed sampling.
Response:
module debouncer(
input wire clk,
input wire reset,
input wire switch,
output reg output
);
// 2^N * 20ns = 10ms
parameter N = 19;
reg [N - 1:0] counter; wire [N - 1:0] counter_next;
wire pause_tick;
parameter [2:0]
  zero = 0,
  wait1_0 = 1,
  wait1_1 = 2,
  test1 = 3,
  one = 4,
  wait0_0 = 5,
  wait0_1 = 6,
  test0 = 7;
reg [2:0] state; reg [2:0] state_next;
  always @(negedge clk, negedge reset) begin
    if((reset == 1'b1)) begin
      state <= zero;
    end else begin
      state <= state_next;
      counter <= counter_next;
    end
  end
  assign counter_next = counter + 1;
  assign pause_tick = (counter == 0) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;
  always @(switch, state, pause_tick) begin
    case(state)
    zero : begin
      if(pause_tick == 1'b1) begin
        state_next <= wait1_0;
      end
    end
    wait1_0 : begin
      if(pause_tick == 1'b1) begin
        state_next <= wait1_1;
      end
    end
    wait1_1 : begin
      if(pause_tick == 1'b1) begin
        state_next <= test1;
      end
    end
    test1 : begin
      if(switch == 1'b1) begin
        output <= 1'b1;
        state_next <= one;
      end
    end
    one : begin
      if(pause_tick == 1'b1) begin
        state_next <= wait0_0;
      end
    end
    wait0_0 : begin
      if(pause_tick == 1'b1) begin
        state_next <= wait0_1;
      end
    end
    wait0_1 : begin
      if(pause_tick == 1'b1) begin
        state_next <= test0;
      end
    end
    test0 : begin
      if(switch == 1'b0) begin
        output <= 1'b0;
        state_next <= zero;
      end
    end
    endcase
  end
endmodule

Instruction: pulse_gen is a retriggerable one-shot that drives pulse_o high for duration_g clock cycles after a strobe. Its inputs are an asynchronous reset, a clock, and a strobe trigger; the output is the generated pulse. While the internal pulse register is high, a 32-bit counter increments until it reaches duration_g-1, then the pulse clears and the counter resets. Asserting the strobe sets the pulse high and clears the counter, restarting the interval.

This module is a MIPS main control decoder: it converts a 6-bit instruction opcode into datapath control signals. Its only input is `opcode`; outputs are 1-bit `Jump`, `Jal`, `Branch`, `Bne`, `MemtoReg`, `MemWrite`, `ALUSrc`, and `RegWrite`, plus 2-bit `RegDst` and 3-bit `ALUOp` (all registered outputs). A combinational `case` decodes opcodes for lw, sw, R-type, addi, andi, ori, xori, slti, j, jal, beq, and bne, assigning each instruction's appropriate control values. Unrecognized opcodes fall through the default case, leaving outputs unchanged.

This module is a parameterized clock frequency divider that generates an output clock whose period is K times the input clock period. It has one input, clkIn, and one registered output, clkOut; K defaults to 2. An internal counter increments on each rising edge of clkIn. When the counter reaches K/2−1, clkOut is driven high; when it reaches K−1, clkOut is driven low and the counter resets to zero, giving a roughly 50% duty cycle.

This module implements an 8-bit rotating LED/shift pattern generator. It has a clock input `clk`, an enable input `E`, and an 8-bit output `Q`. The internal 8-bit register starts at one and, on each rising clock edge while `E` is high, rotates its contents left by one bit, feeding the most significant bit into the least significant bit. `Q` continuously reflects the current register value.

This module implements a 2-to-1 multiplexer. It has two data inputs, i_A and i_B, a select input i_S, and one output o_O. Internally, the output continuously follows i_A when the select is low and i_B when the select is high. The selection is purely combinational.

This module produces a combined active-high reset for an attached IP block. It takes an AXI clock, an active-low AXI reset, and an active-high IP reset input, and drives one reset output. Internally, the active-low AXI reset is inverted and ORed with the IP reset; the result is registered on the rising AXI clock edge, with the AXI reset taking priority to force the output high.

This module implements a combinational half adder. It takes two 1-bit inputs, x and y, and produces two 1-bit outputs: Hsum and Hcarry. Internally, Hsum is computed as the XOR of x and y, yielding the sum bit, while Hcarry is computed as their AND, yielding the carry bit. It has no clock or stored state.

This module is a bank-switching address decoder for a cartridge-based 6502 system. Its inputs are address lines, the data bus, reset, clock, and read/write; its outputs drive cartridge output-enables and ROM selects. It decodes the $8000–BFFF region, selecting cart0/2/4 from bank bits, driving the ROM bank-select from the low bank bit, asserting a shared enable when the bank is 1101, and decoding $FCxx/$FDxx accesses. A 4-bit bank register, reset to a disable-all value, latches D[3:0] on the falling edge of PHI0 when a write to $FEx5 with D[7:4]=0000 occurs. The ROM-strobe output stays inactive.

desxor2 is a purely combinational 32-bit bitwise XOR module, likely used as a DES round helper. It has two 32-bit inputs, d and l, and one 32-bit output, q. Each output bit is the exclusive-OR of the corresponding bits of d and l. There is no clock, reset, or internal state, so q updates immediately when either input changes.

This module bridges an AD and a DA converter, optionally looping the sampled analog input back out. Inputs are Clk, ResetN, Loopthru, 8-bit AD_Input and Data_to_DA; outputs are 8-bit Data_from_AD and DA_Out plus AD_Clk and DA_Clk. A divider generates a slow internal clock (half period of 7 Clk cycles) used as AD_Clk, with DA_Clk its inverse. The AD input is latched on the internal clock's falling edge and DA_Out updated on its rising edge. Loopthru selects between the latched AD data and Data_to_DA.

resultDistributor forwards a 32-bit result word, splitting it into an 8-bit address and 24-bit data. Inputs: clk, vblank, 32-bit resultData, busy. Outputs: 9-bit resultAddr, outputReady strobe, 8-bit outputAddr, 24-bit outputData. Each clock, outputReady is normally low; a rising vblank edge clears the internal counter and pulses outputReady, while a falling busy edge pulses outputReady and increments the counter unless saturated at 255. The counter drives resultAddr; outputAddr and outputData come from resultData's upper 8 and lower 24 bits.

This module is an incomplete building block intended to drive a single output based on a clock and trigger input. Its ports are `clk` and `trig` as inputs, and `data_o` as the output. Internally, a process sensitive to changes on `clk` checks whether `trig` is high, but the conditional body is empty, so no assignment is ever made. As a result, `data_o` is never driven and remains undriven or undefined. The commented-out assignment suggests the intended behavior was to set the output when the trigger is asserted.
Response:
module bug5(
input wire clk,
input wire trig,
output wire data_o
);
  always @(clk) begin
    if((trig == 1'b1)) begin
      //data_o <= '1';  -- uncomment this and everythings's OK
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module implements a 4-bit parallel-in, parallel-out register. It has a 4-bit data input, a 4-bit data output, and a positive-edge clock input. Internally, a 4-bit register initialized to zero is continuously driven onto the output. On each rising clock edge, the register captures the input data, so the output updates synchronously one clock cycle after the input is presented.

A display output switcher for a 6-digit seven-segment readout. Its inputs are sel_raw, sel_decoded, clock dclk, and 20-bit data; outputs are six 4-bit segment drives with enables plus dp. A case statement maps 20-bit codes to an 8-bit command (default EE error marker), split into ones and tens digits. Segments 3–6 show raw data nibbles when sel_raw is set, segment 2 shows either a raw nibble or the decoded ones digit, and segment 1 shows the tens digit when sel_decoded is set. dp follows dclk, inverted when both enables are asserted.

This module implements a 10-bit program counter. Its inputs are a 10-bit load value, output-enable, load-enable, increment-enable, reset, and clock; its outputs are the current count and a tri-state version of that count. Internally, a 10-bit register is updated on clock/control edges, with reset clearing it first, load-enable loading the input value next, and increment-enable adding one otherwise. The count output always reflects the register, while the tri-state output drives it only when output-enable is asserted, otherwise it goes high-impedance.

This module reads a TCP packet from an input FIFO and streams its header and payload. Inputs are the clock, FIFO empty flag, header fields (ports, IP, seq/ack, window, flags, urgent pointer), and payload address/length; outputs are registered header copies, header/data valid strobes, and an 8-bit data bus. A six-state FSM waits for the FIFO, asserts read, latches the header, then emits payload bytes one per cycle while decrementing a byte counter. Payload data is supplied by an internal content memory addressed by an incrementing counter. Headers are emitted without data when the payload length is zero.

This module is a synchronous BCD up-counter that behaves as a minutes:seconds timer, displaying MM:SS and wrapping around after 59 minutes 59 seconds. It takes a clock input `clk`, an active-low reset `rst`, and produces a 16-bit output `s`. Internally, four 4-bit BCD digit registers (seconds units/tens and minutes units/tens) are concatenated to form the output. On each rising clock edge, the seconds-units digit increments, cascading carries when it reaches 9, then seconds-tens at 5, minutes-units at 9, and minutes-tens at 5, which returns the count to zero. Asserting reset clears all four digits.

This module applies a complex rotation correction to an input data stream. It has clock/reset/clear inputs and AXI-Stream-style input/output ports: error, configuration, and data streams in, plus corrected data out with valid/ready/last handshakes. Internally, an inner controller converts the error signal into a phase, a sine/cosine lookup generates a complex correction, and a complex multiplier applies it to the input data. The final output selects the real and imaginary 16-bit lanes from the multiplier’s wide result.
Response:
module controller(
input wire clk,
input wire reset,
input wire clear,
input wire [15:0] i_error_tdata,
input wire i_error_tvalid,
input wire [31:0] i_data_tdata,
input wire i_data_tvalid,
input wire i_data_tlast,
output wire i_data_tready,
input wire [31:0] i_config_tdata,
input wire i_config_tvalid,
output wire i_config_tready,
output wire [31:0] o_data_tdata,
output wire o_data_tvalid,
output wire o_data_tlast,
input wire o_data_tready
);
wire [15:0] phase_tdata;
wire phase_tvalid;
wire phase_tready;
wire [31:0] corrector_tdata;
wire corrector_tvalid;
wire corrector_tready;
wire [79:0] o_data_twidedata;
wire resetn;
  assign resetn =  ~reset;
  // Convert the error signal into a rotation correction signal.
  controller_inner cl(
      .clk(clk),
    .reset(reset),
    .clear(clear),
    .i_error_tdata(i_error_tdata),
    .i_error_tvalid(i_error_tvalid),
    .i_config_tdata(i_config_tdata),
    .i_config_tvalid(i_config_tvalid),
    .i_config_tready(i_config_tready),
    .o_phase_tdata(phase_tdata),
    .o_phase_tvalid(phase_tvalid),
    .o_phase_tready(phase_tready));
  // Convert that phase into a complex signal.
  sincoslut noc(
      .aclk(clk),
    .aresetn(resetn),
    .s_axis_phase_tdata(phase_tdata),
    .s_axis_phase_tvalid(phase_tvalid),
    .s_axis_phase_tready(phase_tready),
    .m_axis_data_tdata(corrector_tdata),
    .m_axis_data_tvalid(corrector_tvalid),
    .m_axis_data_tready(corrector_tready));
  // Multiply the input by the complex correction.
  complex_multiply the_mult(
      .aclk(clk),
    .s_axis_a_tdata(i_data_tdata),
    .s_axis_a_tvalid(i_data_tvalid),
    .s_axis_a_tlast(i_data_tlast),
    .s_axis_a_tready(i_data_tready),
    .s_axis_b_tdata(corrector_tdata),
    .s_axis_b_tvalid(corrector_tvalid),
    .s_axis_b_tready(corrector_tready),
    .m_axis_dout_tdata(o_data_twidedata),
    .m_axis_dout_tvalid(o_data_tvalid),
    .m_axis_dout_tready(o_data_tready),
    .m_axis_dout_tlast(o_data_tlast));
  assign o_data_tdata[31:16] = o_data_twidedata[79:64];
  assign o_data_tdata[15:0] = o_data_twidedata[39:24];
endmodule

Instruction: This module computes the minimum of two unsigned 3-bit numbers, N and M. It takes both values as inputs and produces the smaller one on the 3-bit output min. Internally it derives bitwise equality from XNOR, then uses combinational logic to determine whether N is greater than M, from which a less-than flag is inferred. A final multiplexer selects N when N is less than M, otherwise M; equal inputs return the same value either way.

This module computes the parity of an 8-bit input. It has an 8-bit input `byte` and a single-bit output `paritybit`. Internally, it XOR-reduces all eight input bits and continuously drives the output with that result. The output is therefore high when the input contains an odd number of 1s. The design is purely combinational.

This UART top-level module wraps a receiver and a transmitter to provide full-duplex serial communication with an 8-bit parallel data path. Its ports include the serial transmit output txd_p, serial receive input rxd_p, 8-bit transmit/receive data buses din_p and dout_p, FIFO status/handshake signals empty_p, full_p, re_p, and we_p, plus an error flag, clock, and clock enable. Internally, a counter divides the enabled clock by five to produce the transmitter's bit clock, while the receiver uses the clock enable directly; the busy signal is permanently low.

This module is an 8-bit combinational subtracter. It takes two 8-bit unsigned inputs, A and B, and produces an 8-bit output O. The output is simply the arithmetic difference A minus B, computed continuously via a single continuous assignment. There is no clock, reset, or internal state, so O changes immediately whenever either input changes. Results wrap modulo 256, and the borrow or sign information is not exposed.

This module converts a 7-bit binary input into two 4-bit BCD digits. It has `inBin` as the 7-bit input, plus `outBCD` and `outBCD2` as the unit and tens digit outputs. Internally, the tens digit is derived by comparing the input against ranges of ten, and a corresponding multiple of ten is selected. That value is subtracted from the input to produce the unit digit. The design assumes the input represents a value from 0 to 99.

This module implements an 8-bit registered data path that captures an input value when enabled and clears on reset. Its ports are a clock, active-high asynchronous reset, read enable, 8-bit data input, and 8-bit registered data output. On a rising clock edge, if reset is high the output is asynchronously cleared to zero; otherwise, when read is high the output loads the input value. If read is low, the output holds its previous value.
Response:
module data_safe_8_bit(
input wire clk,
input wire rst,
input wire read,
input wire [7:0] data_in,
output reg [7:0] data_out
);
  always @(posedge clk, posedge rst) begin
    if(rst == 1'b1) begin
      data_out <= {8{1'b0}};
    end else begin
      if((read == 1'b1)) begin
        data_out <= data_in;
      end
    end
  end
endmodule

Instruction: Module dcm2 is a clock-generation wrapper around a Xilinx DCM primitive. It takes one clock input, CLKIN_IN, and produces two outputs: CLK0_OUT and CLKFX_OUT. Internally, the DCM is configured to multiply by 16 and divide by 25 to synthesize CLKFX, while CLK0 is fed back for deskewing. Both DCM clock outputs are routed through global buffers before reaching the module outputs. Reset and phase-shift inputs are tied low, and unused status outputs are left open.

This module converts a 16-bit RGB565 pixel into a 24-bit RGB888 pixel, registering the result on each rising clock edge. It has a clock input, a 16-bit RGB565 input, and a 24-bit RGB888 output. Internally, it splits the input into 5-bit red, 6-bit green, and 5-bit blue fields, then expands each to 8 bits using shifts and bitwise ORs. Red and green use shift-and-OR bit replication, while blue is effectively only left-shifted because both OR terms are identical.

This module is a top-level wrapper that instantiates the configurable Z80CpuMon core to implement a Z80 bus monitor/emulator on a GODIL platform. It exposes the Z80 bus and control interface—clock/reset/wait/interrupt/bus-request signals, M1/MREQ/IORQ/RD/WR/RFSH/HALT/BUSAK, a 16-bit address bus, and bidirectional data—plus mode/trigger inputs, an AVR serial console, switches, LEDs, and test/debug pins. Internally, it maps the board switches to CPU and AVR resets, drives the LEDs from breakpoint and trigger status, and uses the core’s tristate control signals to place MREQ_n, IORQ_n, RD_n, WR_n, and Addr onto the external bus. The Z80CpuMon instance is parameterized for clocking, comparator count, and AVR program memory size, and all Z80, serial, test connector, and debug signals are routed to it.

This module is a trivial single-bit buffer intended to drive output z from input a. It has one input, a, and one output, z. Its only logic is an always block triggered by A that assigns Z from a, but A and Z are not declared and differ in case from the actual ports, so the module as shown would not elaborate correctly in standard Verilog.

This module is a purely combinational LED controller that reflects button presses and simple button-pair combinations. It has a 5-bit input `buttons` and an 8-bit output `leds`. The upper five LEDs directly mirror the five button states. The lower three LEDs indicate pairwise conjunctions: button 0 with button 1, button 2 with button 3, and button 4 with button 0.

This module is a purely combinational pass-through that simply renames an 8-bit bus. Its input is an 8-bit vector declared with indices 0 through 7, and its output is an 8-bit vector declared with indices 8 down to 1. Internally, the output is directly connected to the input with no added logic or state. Because both buses have eight bits, the connection is positional, so corresponding bit positions are mapped even though the declared index ranges differ. It contains no sequential elements.

This module is a self-checking testbench wrapper that exercises a 64-bit-wide, 512-deep first-word-fall-through FIFO. Its only inputs are CLK and RESET, and its outputs are SIM_DONE and STATUS; parameters configure error freezing, stop count, and the random seed. Internally it buffers the clock, synchronizes reset, and instantiates data-generator, data-verifier, and protocol-controller blocks that stimulate and check the FIFO. The controller reports simulation completion and status while the FIFO instance provides full, empty, and program-full indications.

This module computes a jump target address for a processor's program counter. It takes two 32-bit inputs, `instruction` (the current PC value) and `jmp_offset` (the relative offset), and produces the 32-bit output `jmp_adress`. Internally the offset is left-shifted by two bit positions, with the two least-significant bits forced to zero, and the shifted value is added to the base input to form the final address.

This module is a 4-bit multiply-accumulate datapath that registers two input operands, multiplies them, and adds the product to a running 10-bit accumulator each clock. Inputs are the 4-bit operands Ain and Bin, clock CLK, and synchronous clear; outputs are the registered operands Aout and Bout plus the 10-bit sum Result. Internally, two 4-bit registers capture the operands, a MAC unit forms their 8-bit product, and a 10-bit adder combines that zero-extended product with a feedback register holding the accumulator, which clear resets.

This module is a simple reset-key buffer that forwards an external reset signal to the rest of a design. It has one input, `rstkey_port_rst`, and one output, `rstkey_rst`. Internally, there is no sequential or gated logic; the output is directly driven by the input. The module performs no inversion, synchronization, or filtering.

The MEMMUX module is a 16-bit multiplexer that selects the memory output value. Its inputs are 16-bit ALUOUT, DataOUT, and IMOUT, plus control signals ACCMEM and MEM_RAM2; its output is 16-bit MEMOUT. When ACCMEM is 0, MEMOUT follows ALUOUT. When ACCMEM is 1, MEMOUT follows IMOUT if MEM_RAM2 is 1, otherwise it follows DataOUT. For any other ACCMEM value, MEMOUT is driven to zero.
Response:
module MEMMUX(
input wire [15:0] ALUOUT,
input wire [15:0] DataOUT,
input wire ACCMEM,
output reg [15:0] MEMOUT,
input wire [15:0] IMOUT,
input wire MEM_RAM2
);
  always @(ALUOUT, DataOUT, ACCMEM, MEM_RAM2, IMOUT) begin
    case(ACCMEM)
    1'b0 : begin
      MEMOUT <= ALUOUT;
    end
    1'b1 : begin
      if((MEM_RAM2 == 1'b1)) begin
        MEMOUT <= IMOUT;
      end
      else begin
        MEMOUT <= DataOUT;
      end
    end
    default : begin
      MEMOUT <= 16'b0000000000000000;
    end
    endcase
  end
endmodule

Instruction: This module computes the four condition-code flags (NZVC) of a processor status register from an ALU result and operation type. Its inputs are the 32-bit ALU result `alurs`, two operand-derived carry/overflow helpers `ope1` and `ope2`, and the 6-bit `aluop` opcode; the output is the 4-bit registered `nzvc` (negative, zero, overflow, carry). It is purely combinational but declared as a register, re-evaluated on any input change. For add/ADDC-style opcodes it sets N from the result MSB, Z when the result is zero, and derives V and C from `ope1`/`ope2` and the sign bit; subtract opcodes use mirrored logic; logical opcodes set N and Z but force V and C to zero. Unlisted opcodes leave the flags unchanged since there is no else branch for them.

This module implements a simple inferred output buffer. It has one input port `i` and one output port `o`. Internally, the output is directly driven by the input through a continuous assignment, introducing no additional logic or state. It effectively passes the input signal unchanged to the output.

This module is a 30-bit-wide 2-to-1 multiplexer. It has two 30-bit data inputs, IN0 and IN1, a single-bit select input SW, and a 30-bit output REG. Its output continuously follows IN0 when SW is 0 and IN1 when SW is 1. The selection is purely combinational, with no clock or state.

This module is a single-bit synchronous toggle flip-flop with active-high reset. Its ports are clk, rst, and one-bit output q. Internally, a state register is set to the parameter zero (value 1) when rst is high at a rising clock edge; otherwise it toggles between the zero and one parameter values. The output is high only when the state equals the parameter one (value 0), making q the inverse of the state. Thus reset forces q low, and q toggles each clock while reset is low.

The module is a 4-bit bus breakout that bundles four independent single-bit signals into one 4-bit output vector. It has four 1-bit inputs and one 4-bit output. Internally, each input is directly wired to the corresponding output bit, so the module is purely combinational and passes signals through unchanged without logic, inversion, or storage.

The XY2MAP module converts 10-bit VGA pixel coordinates into a 16x16 grid address and a position within that grid cell. Inputs are VGA_X and VGA_Y; outputs are 6-bit GRID_X/GRID_Y and 4-bit BOX_X/BOX_Y. Internally, the upper six bits of each coordinate form the grid index, while the lower four bits form the box offset. This is purely combinational and equivalent to dividing each coordinate by 16.

This module implements a 32-bit equality comparator. It takes two 32-bit inputs, in1 and in0, and produces a single-bit output eq. Internally, it compares the two inputs and drives eq high when they are equal and low otherwise, using a temporary signal to hold the comparison result before driving the output.

This module implements the datapath of a 32-bit pipelined-style processor (SPARC-like) that fetches, decodes, and executes instructions using register-windowed register access. Its ports are a reset input (`Resetext`), a clock input (`Clkinext`), and a 32-bit output `Adressext`, which carries the final write-back data value. Internally it contains program counters, instruction and data memories, a register file with a windows manager, a control unit, an ALU, condition-code/PSR logic, sign extenders, and multiplexers for operand, PC, and write-back selection. The control unit decodes opcode fields to generate register-file, memory, ALU, and PC-source controls, while the ALU result drives both memory addressing and PC branch/jump selection.
